# BOOK FOUR

...it is clear how manifold, how great, and how enormous were the crimes of the Jews committed during the period of the First Temple. For all of those, they were punished by only 70 years in the Babylonian captivity. 

<margin>What was the cause of this most recent captivity.</margin>

However, the Jews of the Second Temple period did not commit so many or such great outrages. For as it is said in the book <term>Yoma</term> <note>The Talmudic tractate "Yoma," meaning "The Day," which discusses the rituals of the Day of Atonement.</note>, in the chapter "Seven Days," they were diligent in the law, in the commandments of God, and in works of mercy; yet they have been punished by this longest and most enduring captivity without mercy. Therefore, since with God—who is most just—the punishment must correspond to the sin, the Jews of our time must necessarily identify a cause for this most recent captivity other than the sins of their ancestors. 

For the earlier Jews, whose crimes were the cause of the destruction of the First Temple, stood in the highest degree (as has been said) as idolaters, killers of prophets, and despisers and rejecters of the divine law. They were full of luxury, avarice, hatred, and countless other crimes, and devoid of works of piety and other good actions, as has now been proved through their own scriptures. 

The later Jews, however, who lived during the time of the Second Temple, it is well established were neither idolaters, nor murderers of prophets, nor so luxurious, nor so greedy, nor infected by such great outrages. On the contrary, they were most diligent in the law, endowed with virtues, and adorned with all good character, as their own scriptures attest. Therefore, they must provide another reason for the overthrow of the Second Temple besides the crimes of those later Jews. This is especially true since divine justice repays each person according to their works, and this most recent captivity, compared to the Babylonian one, is almost infinite. For that earlier one lasted only 70 years despite all those crimes of the ancestors; this one, however, has lasted over 1,460 years so far, and as yet no sign of its end or completion appears. 

For this reason, they can reasonably assign no other cause for it than the death of Jesus of Nazareth, the true Messiah, who was both God and man. For if he had been a mere man, they would not have been struck with such a great and long-lasting punishment because of his death. This, Moses the Egyptian <note>The famous Jewish philosopher Maimonides (1138–1204), often called "Moses Aegyptius" in Latin texts.</note> openly confesses, saying thus in the book of <term>Sophrin</term> <note>A reference to the "Scribes" or perhaps a section of Maimonides' Mishneh Torah; original Hebrew: ישו הנוצרי נראה משיח ונהרג מבית הדין והיה סבה שישראל נהרג בחרב</note>: "Jesus of Nazareth appeared to be the Messiah, and was killed by the house of judgment, and was the cause for Israel to be destroyed by the sword."

<margin>The fifth objection.</margin>
**CAPITO.** Some others also say that for "the righteous," "justice" should be understood in this place. For then the judges and ministers of justice, corrupted by money (as they say), everywhere sold the justice of poor men for a small price.

<margin>Response.</margin>
**GALATINUS.** This interpretation is also perverse. First, because "righteous" and "justice" are different nouns among the Hebrews. For "righteous" is called **tzadik** <note>original: **צדיק** (*tzadik*), meaning a person who is just or righteous.</note>, but "justice" is called **tzedek** <note>original: **צדק** (*tzedek*), the abstract concept of justice or righteousness.</note>. And the text does not say **tzedek** (that is, justice), but **tzadik** (that is, a righteous person). Furthermore, the prophet mentions the selling or trading of this righteous man and the oppression of the poor separately. Moreover, he mentioned the selling or trading of the righteous one first, so that from this he might clearly suggest that the Jews were to suffer this final captivity because they were going to sell, or rather trade for, that Righteous One. If, besides, the "selling of the righteous" was to be understood as the "justice of the poor" which was to be for sale, such a great vengeance would by no means have followed in punishment for this crime. For if punishment is to be inflicted according to the measure of the fault, graver crimes ought to be punished more gravely, while lighter ones should be afflicted with a lighter punishment. It is well established that the selling of a brother, idolatry, and the slaughter of the prophets were graver crimes than the selling of justice for the poor. If therefore the fourth crime was (as they assert) the selling of justice for the poor, it ought not to have been punished more severely than the first three—especially by God, who by His nature is more prone and ready to show mercy than to punish. If, then, the Israelites were punished far more severely, far more bitterly, and far longer for the perpetration of the fourth crime than for the commission of the three preceding ones, it necessarily follows that the fourth crime was something other than the selling of justice for the poor, and much more grave, since its punishment exceeded the punishments of the others almost infinitely. For even if by human law minor sins are sometimes punished more severely, in the Law <note>The text likely refers to the Divine Law or the Torah here.</note>...

Therefore, by the decree of that same Law, he ordered them to be killed with various tortures. For he did not restrain them all with a single penalty, but different types of death were set for each individual. This is a quotation of the law from Deuteronomy 24:7.</note>. They answered him: "That thief shall die." He answered and said: "Where are your fathers who sold their brother <note>Referring to the biblical story of Joseph's brothers selling him into slavery.</note>? You must receive the judgment of heaven upon yourselves. If they were alive, I would have brought their judgment before you, but you shall bear the iniquity of your fathers."

<margin>They were killed by Hadrian Caesar on account of the sale of a righteous man.</margin>
That is, at the beginning of the captivity of Israel, Caesar <note>Hadrian</note> took ten of the elders, who were: Rabbi Ishmael son of Elisha the High Priest; Rabban Simeon son of Gamaliel the Prince; Rabbi Akiba; Rabbi Hanina son of Teradion; Rabbi Chuzpit the Interpreter; Rabbi Elazar son of Shamua; Rabbi Judah son of Dama; Rabbi Yeshevav the Scribe; Rabbi Judah son of Hachinai; and Rabbi Judah son of Baba.

And he said to them: "Judge a judgment of righteousness correctly. If a man is found who has stolen the soul of his brother from the sons of Israel, betrayed him, and sold him, what shall the penalty be?" They answered, saying: "That thief shall die." Caesar responded and said: "And where are your fathers, who sold their brother? You, therefore, must receive the judgment of heaven upon yourselves. If they themselves were living, I would conduct their trial in your presence. You, therefore, shall carry the iniquity of your fathers." All these things are recorded there. And so, because of the crime committed by their fathers in the selling of a righteous man, he caused them to perish by various punishments, as is contained more extensively in that same place. 

In this, it is greatly to be noted that Caesar, wishing to convict them by their own law, proposed the words written in the twenty-fourth chapter of Deuteronomy to them, saying: "If a man be found who has stolen a soul from the sons of Israel, and having betrayed him, sells him, what shall the penalty be?" They, condemning themselves with their own mouths, responded with the words of Deuteronomy immediately following in that same place, saying: "That thief shall die." 

However, the name of this "righteous one," on whose account they were so punished, is not stated there. This is partly because the Talmudists perhaps kept it silent, and partly because—which is more likely—the more recent Jews deleted it from the text. For that reason, the commentaries of their own younger scholars say in that place that the righteous one was Joseph, the son of Jacob, whom his brothers sold into Egypt. They claim that Caesar sought Joseph's blood from them and afflicted them with these kinds of punishments for that reason. 

Thus, so as not to admit the truth <note>Galatinus argues the "truth" is that they are being punished for the "sale" of Jesus, not Joseph.</note>, they are compelled to fall into a most abominable heresy. For when they ask among themselves: "Why did these men, rather than others, bear the punishment for the sin of Joseph's brothers?" and find themselves unable to give any other reason, they say it was a <term>gilgul nephashoth</term> <note>original Hebrew: גילגול נפשות</note>, which is to say, a "revolution" or "reincarnation of souls." They assert that they paid the penalty for the crime of Joseph’s brothers because the souls of those brothers were within them. 

This is surely so absurd that it requires no refutation. For it is not only against the true faith and Holy Scripture, but also against natural reason. It also hardly stands to reason that Caesar would have demanded from them payment for something done at least fifteen hundred years earlier—especially since, at the time Joseph was sold, there was no law by which Caesar could have convicted them as guilty of death. Therefore, it is necessary to conclude...

<summary>Galatinus recounts the Jewish legend of the Ten Martyrs executed by Hadrian, arguing that their death was a divine punishment. He dismisses the Jewish explanation of reincarnation (Gilgul) as a "heresy" used to avoid admitting they were actually being punished for the death of Jesus.</summary>

<meta>This page concludes the argument regarding the "Ten Martyrs." Galatinus identifies the "Righteous One" whose sale brought about the Jewish diaspora as Jesus. [It is ne]cessary that this Righteous One, on account of whose sale and death they were punished with such a cruel slaughter, was none other than Jesus the Nazarene, the true Messiah and true God and man. In vengeance for him, nearly forty years after his death, Jerusalem was utterly overturned, and this most recent captivity of the Jews followed.

### CHAPTER <note>In this dialogue-style text, 'CAP.' refers to the character Capnio (representing the scholar Johannes Reuchlin), and 'GAL.' refers to Galatinus himself.</note>
<margin>Why the Jews were not punished immediately after Christ’s death, but [only] after forty years of captivity.</margin>
For what reason did the vengeance not follow immediately after the death of the Messiah, but only after forty years had passed?

### GALATINUS
It must certainly be considered that this was not done without reason. For God acts patiently, not wishing for anyone to perish, but for all to return to repentance, so that they may finally be saved. Therefore, so that the Jews might have a time for repentance after committing such a great crime, He willed to defer this vengeance for forty years. The ancient Talmudists <note>Scholars of the Talmud, the central text of Jewish civil and ceremonial law.</note> who preceded the coming of Christ also perceived this and, illuminated by the Holy Spirit, predicted it. For our Holy Teacher <note>original Latin: "Rabbenus Haccados," referring to Rabbi Judah the Prince, the 2nd-century editor of the Mishnah.</note>, in the book which he called *Gale Razia* <note>original Hebrew: גלי רזיא, meaning "The Revealer of Secrets." This is a medieval mystical text often cited by Galatinus as if it were ancient.</note>, in the eighth petition, says thus: "Forty years after his passion, God will prolong the destruction, so that He may see whether they will be converted to Him." 

And a little later, wishing to give the reason why God would accept the number forty rather than another number for prolonging the time of punishment, he added these same words: "God will accept the number forty by reason of those forty days during which, having been made man, he remains in his mother’s womb for the formation of his limbs in [relation to] original sin. And because the King Messiah is to come to release this sin and to bring souls into paradise, therefore He will wait forty years, one year for each day. Just as the spies whom Israel sent to investigate the land of promise and to track down the truth stayed forty days on their journey, saying that whatever God had said was false, and therefore they did not want to enter it. All that was a figure <note>A symbolic foreshadowing or "type."</note> of Israel, who would speak against the King Messiah, saying that his promises about bringing them into paradise were false. And for that reason, He will wait forty years, just as He waited for Israel for another forty years in the desert so they would not enter into Jerusalem, one year for every day. Nevertheless, just as those who came after them entered the lower Jerusalem—those who did not harden their hearts like their fathers—so also those who involve themselves in the death of the King Messiah shall not enter the heavenly Jerusalem, except for those who follow [him], if they convert to him and wait forty years." 

All these things were said word-for-word by that Holy Teacher, whom the Jews call "Our Holy Master." If, therefore, the Jews were to undergo this most recent captivity in which they now remain as a punishment for the death of the Messiah (as has been abundantly proved in the preceding three chapters), it is necessarily concluded from what has been said that not only has the time of the Messiah’s first coming already passed, but also that the Messiah himself has already come, and that he was none other than Jesus the Nazarene.

# FOURTH BOOK.

### *The sixth argument showing that the time of the Messiah's first coming has already passed, based on the subjection of the Roman Empire. And first, that the Messiah was to subject the Roman Empire to himself. Chapter 25.*

->CAPNIO.<-
<note>Capnio is the character representing Johannes Reuchlin, a famous 16th-century Christian Hebraist.</note>

Since you wish to prove that the time of the Messiah’s coming has already passed through this sixth argument, it is necessary first to show that the Messiah himself was destined to subjugate the Roman Empire. <margin>GAL.</margin> <note>GAL. refers to Pietro Galatino, the author, acting as the primary speaker.</note> This is most beautifully proven first through the vision of Nebuchadnezzar, King of the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans were the ruling people of the Neo-Babylonian Empire.</note>. For this King (as written in the second chapter of Daniel) saw a certain very large statue, which was composed of various metals. Its head consisted of the finest gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze, its legs of iron, and its feet were partly iron and partly clay. Whereupon Daniel, who was both the identifier and interpreter of the King’s dreams, continues in the Aramaic language: <note>original Aramaic: חזה הוית עד די התגזרת אבן די לא בידין ומחת לצלמא על רגלוהי די פרזלא וחספא והדקת המון</note> That is: "You were looking until a stone was cut out of a mountain without hands, and it struck the statue upon its feet of iron and clay, and crushed them." Afterward, Daniel himself, wishing to explain to the same king what the statue itself designated, added these things among others: <note>original Aramaic: אנת הוא ראשה די דהבא... [to] ...והיא תקום לעלמיא</note> That is: "You are the head of gold. And after you shall rise another kingdom of silver, less than you. Then another, third kingdom of bronze, which shall rule over all the earth. But the fourth kingdom shall be as strong as iron. Just as iron crushes and shatters and tames all things, so it shall crush and tame all these. And whereas you saw the feet and toes were partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; and it shall have something of the firm root of iron in it, just as you saw iron mixed with the clay of the soil. Furthermore, as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, the kingdom shall be partly solid and partly fragile or crushed. Whereas you saw iron mixed with clay, they shall mingle themselves together by the seed of man, but they shall not adhere to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay. And in the days of those kings, the God of heaven shall raise up or establish a Kingdom which shall never be destroyed for all ages. And its kingdom shall not be left to another people; it shall crush and consume all these kingdoms, and it itself shall stand forever."

<summary>Galatinus begins the sixth argument for the Messiah's arrival by interpreting Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the statue in the Book of Daniel, identifying the succession of world empires ending with a Messianic kingdom that shatters the Roman "iron" empire.</summary>

"And his kingdom shall not be handed over to another people. It shall crush and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever." In the preceding words, the great God indicated to King **Nebuchadnezzar** <note>Also spelled Nabuchdononofor; he was the King of Babylon who destroyed the First Temple.</note> through **Daniel** that four kingdoms would succeed one another in the world. For the golden head of the statue he had seen signified himself and his kingdom, that is, the Kingdom of the Chaldeans. The chest and arms of silver represented the kingdom of the Persians and the Medes. The belly and thighs of bronze represented the Greek Monarchy. Furthermore, the iron legs designated the Roman Empire. Then, the mixture of iron and clay in the feet and toes of the statue suggested an alliance of two kingdoms—one strong and the other weak—namely, the Roman and the Jewish, arising from the "plant of iron," that is, by the permission of the Roman Empire.

Finally, by the stone cut from the mountain without hands, which, by striking the iron and clay feet of the statue, crushed it and reduced it to dust, it is shown that the Messiah was designated, who was to subject the Roman Empire to himself. Moreover, the mountain from which that stone was cut figured the mother of the Messiah himself, who, on account of the excellence of her virtues, is not inaptly compared to a mountain. But because the Messiah was to be born of a virgin mother, he therefore said this stone was cut from the mountain by itself, without hands—that is, without human embraces—to designate that the body of the Messiah was to be formed without male seed, by the sole cooperation of the Holy Spirit, from the most pure blood of the Virgin.

He showed that the birth and arrival of this Messiah would occur while the mixture of iron and clay lasted—that is, while the alliance of Roman and Jewish power remained—when he said: "And in the days of those Kings, the God of heaven will raise up (or establish) a Kingdom which shall not be scattered forever (that is, unto eternity). And his kingdom shall not be handed over to another people. It shall crush and consume all these kingdoms, and it itself shall stand (that is, endure) forever (that is, unto eternity)." <gloss>Commentary of Rabbi Abraham: This is the kingdom of the Messiah.</gloss> <note>Rabbi Abraham refers to Abraham Ibn Ezra, a celebrated 12th-century Jewish scholar and biblical commentator.</note> Finally, **Daniel** concludes, saying:

Inasmuch as you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and it crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God has made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter. And the dream is true, and its interpretation is faithful. <note>original Aramaic: כל קבל די חזיתא די מטורא אתגזרת אבן די לא בידין והדקת פרזלא נחשא חספא וכספא ודהבא אלה רב הודע למלכא מה די להוא אחרי דנא ויציב חלמא ומהימן פשרה</note>

These things are clearly evident from the explanation of what was said before. Moreover, these points are excellently confirmed by what is found in the <term>Midrash Tehillim</term> <note>A "Midrash" is a form of Jewish commentary; "Tehillim" is the Hebrew name for the Book of Psalms.</note>, that is, in the exposition of the <term>Psalms</term>, upon the title of <term>Psalm 17</term>. Where it is said: "When the Messiah comes with speed, there will be none singing a song." And further down: "Until there falls before him the one having toes, namely the wicked Kingdom, that is, the Roman, of which it was said in <term>Daniel 2</term>: 'And the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of clay; the kingdom shall be partly strong and partly brittle.' And in the days of those Kings, the God of heaven will raise up (or establish) a kingdom which shall not be scattered forever."

### That the Messiah was to rule the whole world, and concerning the universal Kingdom of our Lord Jesus Christ. Chapter XXVI.

The third king was **Joseph**. The fourth king was **Solomon**, King of Israel. The fifth king was **Nebuchadnezzar**, King of Babylon. The tenth king, however, is the **King Messiah**, who shall reign from one end of the world to the other, just as it is said in Psalm 72: "And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth." Likewise, another scripture says in Daniel chapter 2: "And the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth." **GALATINUS.** This will indeed be easy, my dear *Capnio* <note>The Greek-derived nickname for Johann Reuchlin, meaning "smoky."</note>, if we first show that it is entirely false to understand *Rome*, or the *Roman* people, by the "daughter of *Edom*" in this passage. ### BOOK FOUR

...yours, says the Lord God. From these things, therefore, it is clearly evident that it was not without cause that the Romans were mystically and metaphorically called the sons of Esau and Edom in former times.

**CAP.** Why were the Romans metaphorically called Edom and the sons of Esau in former times?

**GAL.** Because of imitation, I say. For not only they, but also all others who persecuted the people of God and offered worship to idols, were called Edom and Esau "according to the flesh" by the ancient Jews, because they imitated their works. This seems sufficiently clear from the fact that in the book *Avoda Zara* <term>Avoda Zara: A tractate of the Talmud concerning "Foreign Worship" or idolatry.</term>—that is, foreign service, or idolatry—it is read thus regarding that saying in the last chapter of Obadiah: *And there shall not be a remnant for the house of Esau.* <note>original Hebrew: "ולא יהיה שריד לבית עשו"</note> This means: *And there shall not be a remnant for the house of Esau*—that is, for those doing the works of Esau. It is also handed down in this way: *And there shall not be a remnant for the house of Esau.* Can this be said of everyone? The tradition teaches it should be said of the *house of Esau*—that is, for everyone doing the work of Esau. This is the tradition. From these things it is manifest enough that the Jews of our time lie when they call Christians "Edom" or "sons of Esau," since Christians do not imitate their works in the least. Rather, the Romans themselves ceased to be Edom and sons of Esau when they became Christians. For then that saying of Micah 5 was fulfilled: *And the remnant of their brothers shall be converted to the house of Israel.* <note>Micah 5:3.</note> Therefore, to return to the previously mentioned prophecy of Jeremiah, we say that in truth, the "daughter of Edom" is the kingdom of Idumea <note>An ancient region south of the Dead Sea inhabited by Edomites.</note>, so named from that same Edom, and "Uz" is a city situated in that same kingdom. And therefore Edom is said to dwell in the land of Uz, because that city of Uz was famous throughout that whole kingdom.

**CAP.** If a Jew should perhaps say: "Since the 'daughter of Edom' is properly the kingdom of Idumea, and you Christians say this prophecy has been fulfilled, when then was it fulfilled?"

**GAL.** The ancient Jews say that this prophecy was fulfilled in the time of King Hyrcanus the Maccabee <note>John Hyrcanus I, a Hasmonean leader who ruled Judea from 134–104 BC.</note>. For then that whole land was destroyed. From there, Hyrcanus himself led out, among others, four thousand captives to guard the walls of the city of Jerusalem.

<margin>Josephus, *Antiquities*, Book 13</margin>
Wherefore, as Josephus says, on that day there was great joy among the Jews. So much so that, as Rabbi Yehoshua son of Levi reports, no joy in the Temple was ever greater than that one. This was because Beth-shean <note>A significant ancient city in Israel.</note> and the other cities of the Idumeans—which could not be conquered in the time of Joshua, nor in the time of the Judges, nor in the time of the kings of Israel and Judah—were conquered in the time of this King Hyrcanus and subjected to the rule of the Jews.

<margin>Josephus, *Antiquities*, Book 13, Chapter 17</margin>
Josephus says, moreover, that those of Edom, the sons of Esau, were converted to Judaism in the time of the aforementioned King Hyrcanus, and were circumcised; they did not withdraw from the Jews even in the time of Vespasian and Titus <note>The Roman emperors who oversaw the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD.</note>, but always remained Jews thereafter. Therefore we say that the sin of the Jewish "sons of Esau" was then remembered, and they fell into captivity, at the time when the iniquity of the sons of Judah—those who remained righteous at the coming of the Messiah, Jesus the Nazarene—was completed.

...rather, on the contrary, we say that the Jews themselves are of Edom—those who were converted to them from Edom, and those who are wicked and sinners. Together with them, they have received a perpetual punishment in which they now remain, and will remain until the end of the world. But we say that the Christians are the "sons of Zion" and are the "good Jews" who turned to Christ. In them, iniquity has been completed—that is, sin and captivity have ceased—and they will be free forever, as is clearly evident in the aforementioned prophecy. For concerning those converted from Edom to Judaism, and the rest of the Jews who deny Christ, the prophet says: *The cup shall also pass to you* <note>original Latin: "Ad te quoq̃ peruenit calix". A reference to Lamentations 4:21.</note>—that is, the punishment of divine vengeance. *You shall be drunken*—that is, you shall be fully punished—*and you shall be made naked*—that is, you shall be deprived of honor, dignities, and other goods. It is certain that this was done through Titus, the prince of the Romans <note>Titus (reigned 79–81 AD) was the Roman general who besieged and destroyed Jerusalem and its Temple in 70 AD.</note>. For that people of Zion, believing in Christ, was never again subjected to any captivity—speaking of the people as a whole—just as has happened three times now to the people of the Jews. Therefore, he subsequently says: *He will no longer carry you away into exile*—namely, from liberty into slavery. It follows regarding the wicked Jews, the children of Edom: *He will visit your iniquity, O daughter of Edom*—namely, by punishing her justly. *He will uncover your sins*—namely, by bringing upon you a punishment manifest to all. For their captivity and servitude is public throughout the whole world. For wherever the Jews dwell, whether among Christians or among Saracens <note>A common medieval and Renaissance term for Muslims.</note>, they are always captives and always held in abomination. From these points, the solution to the Jews' argument is clear.

<margin>
An objection of the modern Jews.
</margin>

**CAP.** The Jews still insist. Since the Roman kingdom is the fourth among the other kingdoms foretold by Daniel <note>In the Book of Daniel, four great empires are prophesied to rise before the kingdom of God is established. Christian tradition usually identifies these as Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, and Rome.</note>, after which the kingdom of the Messiah was to succeed—a kingdom that would never end—and since the Roman Empire still perseveres (because Roman Emperors and Kings have never ceased), they therefore conclude that the Messiah has not yet arrived. **GAL.**

<margin>
The Response.
</margin>

Just as the intention of the prophet Daniel in predicting the destruction of the kingdom of the Chaldeans <note>The Neo-Babylonian Empire.</note> was not that no one would ever rule in Babylonia again, but rather that no one of the lineage of Nebuchadnezzar, nor of his nation, would rule there from then on (which is why the kingdom of the Chaldeans was said to have failed then); so too in the cessation of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, the intention of the prophet himself was not that no one would rule in Media and Persia thereafter, but that no one from then on of the lineage or nation of Darius regarding the kingdom of the Medes, nor of the lineage or nation of Cyrus regarding the kingdom of the Persians, would be ruler. So also in the failing of the kingdom of the Greeks, the intention of the same prophet was not that no one would rule in Greece from then on, but that no one of the lineage of Alexander, nor of his nation, would be king any longer. Thus also it must be said regarding the failing of the Roman kingdom, that the intention of the aforementioned prophet was not that no one would rule at Rome any longer, but that no one from then on...

# Book Five.

## In which the objections of the Jews of our time, who strive to prove that the Messiah has not yet come, are most effectively refuted.

### Objections of the more recent Jews: That Jesus of Nazareth was not the Messiah, since the Messiah himself has not yet come. Chapter 1.

-> CAPNIO, <-
<note>Capnio is the Greek-style pseudonym of the famous German Hebraist Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), who appears as a character in this dialogue.</note>

**S**ince little or no benefit is brought to the Christian faith—and indeed, a very great danger to Catholic truth often arises—by those who, although they refute the errors of the enemies of the faith with strong reasons, are nevertheless completely ignorant of the falsehoods with which those enemies attack the truth of our faith. For what does it profit to strike the enemy bravely, unless his strengths and all his crafts of doing harm are also known, so that his blows may be either providently avoided or received without injury? For that reason, if you desire to perform a worthwhile service for the followers of Christ, you should endeavor to refute with all zeal and all diligence the objections of the Jews of our time, by which they strive to subvert the truth.

-> GALATINO <-
<note>Galatino refers to the author, Pietro Galatino, a Franciscan friar and scholar of Hebrew.</note>

You, therefore, who are most skilled in their language <note>original: "linguam," referring to Hebrew</note>, have often read their books, and have always detested their customs, should bring forward into the open whatever arguments they strive to make against us; I, for my part, will take care to resolve each of them through their own scriptures.

-> CAPNIO <-

...we shall walk in his paths. For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of God from Jerusalem. <margin>First objection.</margin> 
And first indeed they argue así: When the prophet says, "And it shall be in the end of days," his word is understood to be fulfilled in the days of the Messiah. The Messiah, therefore, was to come in the end of days. But your Christ did not come in the end of days, since many days have passed since his coming. Therefore, he himself was not the Messiah.

<margin>Second.</margin> 
Then indeed así: What the prophet says, "The mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of the mountains." This has not yet happened. For we have not yet seen the mountain of the temple of the Lord raised above the tops of the mountains. Therefore, the Messiah has not yet come.

<margin>Third.</margin> 
Thirdly thus: When the prophet says, "And all nations shall flow to him," he predicted that all nations would flow together to the Messiah. Since, therefore, all nations have not flowed to him whom you say was the Messiah—for neither the Saracens <note>A medieval term for Muslims.</note>, nor the Tartars <note>A term often used for the Mongol and Turkic peoples of Central Asia.</note>, nor many others have run to him through faith—it follows that he was not the Messiah himself.

<margin>Fourth.</margin> 
Afterward, when the prophet says, "And many peoples shall go and say, Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob." This was by no means fulfilled at the coming of Jesus of Nazareth. For some of those who believe in him say, "Let us go to the house of Peter." Others, "Let us go to the house of Paul." Others, "Let us go to the house of Francis." Others, "Let us go to the house of Anthony," <note>Referring to the popular devotion to saints like St. Francis of Assisi and St. Anthony of Padua, which the objectors argue replaces the focus on the God of Jacob.</note> and so on for the rest. But no one says, "Let us go to the house of the God of Jacob." For which reason it is clear that Jesus of Nazareth himself was not the Messiah.

<margin>Fifth.</margin> 
Fifth, when he says, "And they shall beat, or hammer, or crush their swords into plowshares," along with the rest. From these things (they say) it is clear that such great peace was to exist in the days of the Messiah that men would convert weapons of war into instruments of agriculture, and that nation would no longer lift up the sword against nation. And consequently, that peace would last without end. Since, therefore, nothing of the sort has ever happened—rather, after he came whom you assert to be the Messiah, wars have been carried on just as they were carried on before. And perhaps it is certain that many more, and much greater and fiercer battles have occurred after Jesus himself than occurred before him. 

<margin>Sixth.</margin> 
Therefore, he himself was not the Messiah. Finally, from what he says, "Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn war anymore," they infer that the Messiah has not yet come, because peace without end has not yet been established in the world. They also bring against us those words of the same prophet Isaiah, when in the eleventh chapter he says again:

->*Regarding the first objection of the Jews, that the Messiah was to come at the end of days. Chapter 11.*<-

->GALATINUS,<-

**TO** the first of these objections, therefore, by which the younger Jews attempt to conclude that the Messiah has not yet come, and consequently that our Lord Jesus was not the Messiah, because according to the aforementioned prophecies of Isaiah and Micah, the Messiah himself was to come in the end or in the last of days. We say that no reason compels "the end" or "the last of days" in the aforementioned words to designate the end of mankind or the end of the world, but rather the end of those things to which the prophets themselves were speaking. For the "end of days" is said there to be that time which was from the time of Cyrus, king of the Persians, until the destruction of the second temple. This is most clearly evident from what is read in Jeremiah 49: "And it shall be in the end of days I will bring back the captivity of Elam, says the Lord." <note>original Hebrew: *והיה באחרית הימים אשיב את שבות עילם נאם יהוה*</note> For Elam was a region of Persia, where Cyrus, who...

granted indulgence to the Jews to return, as is evident from the first chapter of Ezra. Therefore, the **end of days** of which the prophet spoke was the time and state of the Second Temple. In that period, all their good vanished, and every irrevocable evil came upon them, as has been shown more extensively in the preceding pages. For then, as the day ended, the evening came, which is the end of the day; their sun set, and darkness fell upon them, and baldness <note>In biblical terms, baldness often signifies a period of intense mourning or divine judgment.</note> descended upon their heads, because they denied the Messiah of the Lord.

That the evening and darkness came upon them as the day receded is found in the *Commentaries on Genesis* by Rabbi Moses Hadarsan <note>Moses ha-Darshan was an 11th-century Jewish scholar from Narbonne, famous for his collection of midrashic (interpretive) stories; he is frequently quoted in medieval Christian-Jewish debates.</note>, regarding that statement in the 30th chapter of the same book: *And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, to call him.* <note>original Hebrew: ויבא יעקב מן השדה בערב ותצא לאה לקראתו</note> For it is said there: This is what is written in Psalm 104: *You make darkness, and it is night, wherein all the beasts of the forest creep forth. The young lions roar after their prey, and seek their food from God. The sun rises, they gather themselves together.* <note>original Hebrew: תשת חשך ויהי לילה בו תרמש כל חיתו יער הכפירים שאגים לטרף ולבקש מאל אכלם : תזרח השמש יאספון</note> This means: **You make darkness**—that is, the captivity of Israel—when their works have become dark, according to that saying in Isaiah 29: *And their works were in the dark.* <note>original Hebrew: וחיה במחשך מעשיהם</note> Therefore, God shall darken the world against them. Just as it is said in the 2nd chapter of Joel: *The sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining.* <note>original Hebrew: שמש וירח קדרו וככבים אספו נגהם</note> It follows: **And it shall be night.** These are the days of captivity, which are like night to Israel. **In it creep all the beasts of the forest.** These are the nations of the world, who are called "beasts of the forest" because they creep forth to trample Israel, as it is said in Psalm 79: *The boar out of the wood wastes it, and the wild beast of the field devours it.* <note>original Hebrew: יכרסמנה חזיר מיער וזיז שדי ירענה</note> It follows: **The young lions roar after their prey.** These young lions are the Gentiles, who deny the Holy and Blessed God and roar to seize their prey.

Rabbi Hanina said: These are the ones who deny God and roar for prey, yet they nevertheless demand a reward from God in the future. <margin>*Col*, a Hebrew word.</margin>
To their third objection, from which they infer that our Lord Jesus of Nazareth was not the Messiah because all nations did not flow to him, a response of this kind is given: The Hebrew word <term>Col</term> <note>original Hebrew: "כל"</note>—which is the same as "all," "every," "whole," or "universal"—is not used as strictly by the prophets and theologians as it is by the <term>dialecticians</term> <note>Logic scholars or philosophers who used terms with mathematical precision.</note>. Although many examples of this are found in Holy Scripture, it is sufficient to bring forward a few. For in the Second Book of Kings <note>Known as 2 Samuel in modern Bibles.</note>, chapter 16, we read as follows: <note>original Hebrew: "ויבא אבשלום אל פלגשי אביו לעיני כל ישראל"</note> **And Absalom went in to his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.** <note>2 Samuel 16:22</note> And again in chapter 17 of the same book: <note>original Hebrew: "ויאמר אבשלום וכל איש ישראל טובה עצת חושי הארכי מעצת אחיתפל"</note> **And Absalom and every man of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better—that is, more good—than the counsel of Ahithophel."** <note>2 Samuel 17:14</note> Behold, therefore, how the Scripture places this word "all" in both instances. Yet no one would be so foolish as to say that not a single person from Israel was missing there, or that there was no one who failed to see Absalom when he committed that disgrace, or who did not approve of the counsel of Hushai the Archite. For although the Scripture says "all Israel" and "every man," it is reasonable to believe that many more people of Israel were absent than were present, considering those who were with David and those in all the borders...

The original Hebrew is: כָּל מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ וְגַלֶּיךָ עָלַי עָבָרוּ</note> That is, all your crushing depths and your floods have passed over me. Therefore, when the Scripture speaks in this way, this word "all" is very often understood to mean "many" rather than "each and every single one." Rabbi Kimhi <note>David Kimhi (c. 1160–1235), also known as Radak, a famous medieval Jewish grammarian and biblical commentator.</note> explains this very well in his book *The Roots*, <note>original: "Seraffim," a corruption of the Hebrew "Sefer ha-Shorashim" (The Book of Roots), Kimhi's famous Hebrew dictionary.</note> saying: **kol**, that is "all," is a word that encompasses individuals, but sometimes it refers only to a large part of a multitude. As in that passage from Genesis 41: **And all the earth came to Egypt.** <note>Genesis 41:57. Hebrew: וכל הארץ באו מצרימה</note> And again in chapter 24: **And all the goods of his master were in his hand.** <note>Genesis 24:10. Hebrew: וכל טוב אדניו בידו</note> Likewise in 4 Kings, chapter 8: **And he took a gift in his hand, and all the goods of Damascus.** <note>2 Kings 8:9 in modern Bibles. Hebrew: ויקח מנחה בידו וכל טוב דמשק</note> Thus says Rabbi Kimhi.

The same is also clearly evident from the *Midrash Shir ha-Shirim* <note>A traditional rabbinic commentary on the Song of Songs.</note>—that is, from the exposition of the Song of Songs—when discussing the verse in chapter 2: **The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.** <note>Song of Songs 2:8</note> It is said there: "There are no mountains here except for idolatries." This is what was said in Hosea, chapter 4: **They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills.** <note>Hosea 4:13</note> Rabbi Yoden and Rabbi Huna said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer: **The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.** This refers to the King Messiah. For in the hour that he comes, he shall say to Israel: "In this month you shall be redeemed." But they will say to him: "Our master, King Messiah, how can we be redeemed? Did not God, holy and blessed, swear that he would make us serve seventy nations?" <note>In rabbinic tradition, the world is said to be comprised of seventy nations.</note> But he will give them two answers, saying: "If one of you is taken captive among the Sarmatians <note>An ancient nomadic people from the region of modern-day Ukraine and Russia.</note> and another in Africa, it is the same as if he had held all of you captive. Not only this, but this wicked kingdom—that is, the Roman Empire—enrolls soldiers for its service from every nation in the world and from each one of them. Thus, a single Cuthæan <note>Historically a Samaritan, but often used in such texts to mean a generic foreign soldier or official.</note> comes and conscripts you; a single 'Sarchius' <note>Likely referring to a Saracen.</note> comes and conscripts you; an Ethiopian comes and conscripts you; one from Persia comes and conscripts you; until every nation under his rule has conscripted you and forced you to serve. Therefore, it is as if you had served seventy nations. And in this month—that is, the month of Passover—you shall be redeemed." As it is said in Exodus 12. This is the tradition.

From these things, therefore, it is clear that this Hebrew word **kol** (all) is frequently understood to mean "many" rather than "all and every single one." This manner of speaking is also commonly used by everyone else. For when a large part of the people of a city go to some spectacle, we say "the whole city" or "all the people" went...

Therefore, according to this and according to their own tradition, it can rightly be said that even if no others had believed in our Savior except the Romans, "all nations" would have flowed to him. Therefore, this foolish objection of the Jews detracts in no way from our Savior.

### To the fourth objection of the Jews: That the Messiah has not yet come because the nations have not yet said, "Come, let us go up to the house of the God of Jacob." Chapter 5.

# GALATINO,

->*To the fifth objection of the Jews: That the Messiah has not yet come because the weapons of war have not yet been converted into agricultural instruments. Chapter VI.*<-

## GALATINVS,

Their fifth objection—when they strive to conclude from the words of the same prophet that the Messiah has not yet come because swords have not yet been turned into mattocks <note>original Latin: *ligones*; often translated as plowshares in this biblical context</note> nor spears into pruning hooks <note>original Latin: *falces*; sickles or curved blades for pruning</note>—is refuted by their own <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism, consisting of the Mishnah and the Gemara.</note>. For a certain tradition of theirs shows that the world was not to be so drastically altered as they ignorantly, or rather deceitfully, claim. This tradition, in the book <term>Sabbath</term> <note>original Hebrew: שבת (*Shabbat*); the Talmudic tractate dealing with Sabbath laws</note>, that is, of the Sabbath, says the following: "The masters have handed down that no one should go out on the Sabbath day with a sword or other weapons. However, Rabbi Eliezer says that weapons are ornaments for a man." They said to him therefore: "Since they are ornaments for a man, for what reason will they cease in the days of the Messiah?" He answered them: "Because they will not be necessary. As it is said in Isaiah chapter 2: *And nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war anymore.*" They said to him: "They will at least be for ornament or beauty." But Rabbi <term>Abaya</term> <note>original Hebrew: אביי (*Abaye*); a prominent 4th-century Babylonian scholar</note> said: "To what purpose? For what use would they be, like a lamp at noon?" <note>Meaning they would be redundant or useless, as a lamp is unnecessary in broad daylight.</note> 

However, Rabbi Samuel held the opposite opinion. For he says: "There is no difference between this age and the days of the Messiah, except only for the servitude to kingdoms." <note>This is a famous Talmudic dictum suggesting that the Messianic era is not a supernatural change in nature, but a political change in Jewish sovereignty.</note> As it is written in Deuteronomy 15: *For the poor will never cease from the midst of the land.* And a little later it follows thus: "And there were those who said that they spoke to him (that is, to Rabbi Eliezer): 'Since weapons are an ornament to a man, why then will they cease in the days of the Messiah?' He answered them: 'Even in the days of the Messiah weapons will not cease, but they will cease in the future coming.'" Thus far the Talmud. 

Where it should be noted that the same Rabbi who just before seemed to assert that weapons ought to have ceased in the days of the Messiah, here explaining himself, recalls what he had said: namely, that they are not to cease at the first coming of the Messiah, but in the future coming, that is, in his second coming. There is also a second point: that where this tradition says "there is no difference between this age and the days of the Messiah, except the servitude to kingdoms," the sense is that the servants of the Messiah and those believing in him were no longer to serve the kings of idolatrous nations. # Chapter 7. Regarding the sixth objection: That the Messiah has not yet come, because peace without end has not yet arrived.

### GALATINUS

The sixth objection of theirs is completely emptied of force through their own scriptures. For they argue that since the prophet says, *Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, nor shall they learn war anymore* <note>Isaiah 2:4</note>, the Messiah has not yet come, because peace without end has not yet reached the world. However, the words of the prophet himself seem to sound as if a perpetual peace ought to happen in the days of the Messiah. One must respond to them according to how these words are explained in the Talmud by their own wise men. 

First, it should be noted that this word *od* <note>Hebrew: עוד, typically meaning "yet," "again," or "anymore."</note>, which we translate as "anymore" or "further," even if it is sometimes (though rarely) taken for "never" or "ever"—as in Genesis chapter 8: *I will not furthermore add to curse the earth*—and again in chapter 9: *And there shall not be furthermore a flood*—it nevertheless frequently signifies a very brief time. This is taught by Rabbi Kimhi <note>David Kimhi (c. 1160–1235), a highly influential medieval Jewish grammarian and biblical commentator known as the Radak.</note> in the book *Shorashim* <note>original: "Serassim"; the "Book of Roots," a standard Hebrew dictionary of the era.</note>, saying: "It happens that this word *od*, that is 'furthermore,' signifies a small time." 

As when it is said in Proverbs chapter 31: *Give strong drink to the one who is perishing, and wine to him who is bitter in soul. He shall drink and forget his poverty, and his labor he shall not remember furthermore.* For "furthermore" there does not signify "ever" or "into eternity," but only as long as the wine is in him. So too that saying in 2 Kings chapter 6: *And the raiding bands of Syria did not add to come furthermore into the land of Israel*—that is, at that time. 

Likewise, it sometimes happens that *od* signifies *addaim*, which is "as of yet." As in Psalm 88: *Free among the dead, like the slain sleeping in the grave, of whom you have not been mindful furthermore.* As if to say, you have not been mindful of them "as of yet," until the time comes in which the memory of the dead shall occur, so that they may rise. And so it is also in Job chapter 2: *Do you still hold fast to your integrity?* 

Thus far Rabbi Kimhi. From his words, it is clear enough that this Hebrew word *od* is indeed rarely taken for "ever" or "further," but is frequently taken for a determined or even a brief period. But since the Jews—as is their habit—still argue contentiously despite what has been said, we must again turn some of their own arrows <note>original: "spicula"; literally "little stings" or "darts," a common rhetorical term for turning an opponent's arguments against them.</note> back against them. 

Let one of these be what is found in Genesis chapter 35: *And God said to him, "Your name is Jacob; your name shall not be called Jacob furthermore, but Israel shall be your name."* Here, let Jewish perversity look more closely. Because just as it was said...

### *Regarding the eighth objection of the Jews, that the Messiah has not yet come because they are not yet gathered into their own land. Chapter IX.*

-> CAPNIO, <-
<note>Capnio is the Greek-derived nickname of Johannes Reuchlin (1455–122), a famous German humanist and scholar of Hebrew.</note>

**A**s a culmination of their falsehood and blindness, they still take up another argument from what is read in the thirtieth chapter of *Deuteronomy*: <term>Then the Lord your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you and gather you again from all the peoples where the Lord your God scattered you. (v’shav Adonai Elohekha et shevutkha...)</note>. This means: And the Lord your God will turn back your captivity, and have mercy on you. Since, therefore (they say), more than one thousand four hundred years have passed since we were scattered throughout the world, and we are to be led back and gathered into the land which our fathers possessed by the Messiah when he comes—just as it has been handed down to us from our fathers, and as has been prophesied many times both by Moses in the words mentioned above and by other prophets—it is manifest from this that the Messiah himself has not yet come, and consequently your Jesus was not the Messiah. <margin>Who the true Jews are.</margin>
Thus far Rabbi Moses Hadarsan. From this tradition, therefore, it clearly appears that in the aforementioned words of Jeremiah, when he says, *In his days Judah shall be saved*, "Judah" is understood not for the unbelieving Jews who deny the true Messiah, but for all people whatsoever who confess the Savior himself.

<margin>How Judah is interpreted.</margin>
And it appears that all who confess him in heart, word, and deed, shall be saved. For *Judah* is interpreted as the *acknowledgment of God*. For *Yah* <note>Hebrew: יה</note> is the same as "God," and *hoda* <note>Hebrew: הודה</note> means "confession" or "acknowledgment." From these is composed *Yehudah* <note>Hebrew: יהודה</note>, that is, Judah, which is the same as "Acknowledgment of God." It is also read in Hosea chapter 1: *I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, for I will utterly forget them. But I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God. And I will not save them by bow, or by sword, or by battle, nor by horses or horsemen.* <note>original Hebrew: לא אוסיף עוד ארחם את בית ישראל כי נשא אשא להם ואת בית יהודה ארחם והושעתים ביהוה אלהיהם ולא אושיעם בקשת ובחרב ובמלחמה ובסוסים ובפרשים</note>

Which Rabbi Jonathan <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, to whom the Aramaic translation (Targum) of the Prophets is traditionally attributed.</note> thus translated and explained in Aramaic: *Behold, I will not add more to have mercy on the house of Israel. However, if they repent, I will surely forgive them. But I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them by the Word of the Lord their God. And they shall not be saved by the bow, or by the sword, or by those making war with horses and horsemen.* <note>original Aramaic: לא אוסיף עוד לרחמא על בית ישראל ברם אם יתובון משבק אשבק להון ועל דבית יהודה ארחם ואפרקינון במימרא דיהוה אלההון ולא יתפרקון בקשתא ובחרבא ובעבודי קרבא ובסוסון ובפרשין</note> Now, that the Messiah is the "Word of God" <note>The Aramaic term "Memra" (Word) was used in the Targums to describe God's interaction with the world; the author identifies this specifically with Jesus as the Logos.</note> was seen at great length in the third book.

<margin>The House of Judah is the Church of Christians.</margin>
From these words it is also manifest that the "House of Judah" on whom God was to have mercy, and whom he was to save by his Word—that is, through the Messiah his Son—is understood as the Church of Christ; that is, the congregation of the faithful who acknowledge Christ as the true Son of God, and not the unbelieving...

### To the eleventh Jewish objection: That the Messiah has not yet come because Gog has not yet been slain, nor Magog conquered. Chapter 12.

->CAPNIO,<-
<note>Capnio is the Greek-derived pen name of Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a pioneering German humanist and scholar of Hebrew who is a central character in this work.</note>

The Jews further object against us, and against our Lord the true Messiah, another argument based on those things which are read in the Holy Scriptures concerning Gog and Magog, and especially in Ezekiel chapter 38, which says: *Son of man, set your face toward Gog, of the land of Magog.* <note>original Hebrew: בן אדם שים פניך אל גוג ארץ המגוג</note> Where the gloss of Rabbi Solomon says: Gog is the name of the king, and Magog is the name of the nation. This is indicated by the word *sanim* <note>original: שנים. This Hebrew word can be read as *shanim* (years) or *shenaim* (two).</note> spoken here. You should not say *sanim* (years), but *senaim* (two). For two prophets <note>Referring to Eldad and Medad.</note> announced one prophecy at that time. Thus far Rabbi Solomon.

From these things, therefore, and from others which *Ezekiel* himself mentions in chapter 39 concerning *Gog* and *Magog*, the younger generation of Jews take an argument for their own wickedness, saying: That through the *Messiah*, God is to fight against *Gog* and *Magog*, and he is to slay *Gog* himself, according to that saying of *Isaiah*: *And with the spirit of his lips he shall slay the wicked* <note>original Latin: "Et spiritu labiorum suorum occidet impium"; see Isaiah 11:4.</note>; and that he is to lead us back into our own land, to reign forever with him in *Jerusalem*. ->GALATINUS<- 

Since no third temple is to be built (as was shown more extensively in the preceding sections), and the Jews are never going to possess their own land again, nor are the ten tribes ever to return (as will be shown most extensively in what follows), we therefore say that the aforementioned words of *Ezekiel*, and whatever else is read anywhere concerning *Gog and Magog*, are to be understood not according to the letter, but spiritually. Moreover, that the ten tribes are never to return is now shown through that which is read in the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter *Helec* <note>The eleventh chapter of the Talmudic tractate Sanhedrin, which discusses who has a portion in the World to Come.</note>, in this manner: "The ten tribes are not in the future to return." That is, they are never to return to the land of *Israel*. The *Rabbanan* <note>A term for "The Rabbis" or "The Teachers."</note> have handed down: "The ten tribes will have no part in the world to come." Just as it is said in *Deuteronomy 29*: *And the Lord uprooted them out of their land in anger, and in wrath, and in great indignation.* <note>original Hebrew: ויתשם יהוה מעל אדמתם באף ובחמה ובקצף גדול</note> This is the tradition. 

Since, therefore, the third temple is not to be built, nor are the Jews ever again to return to their land, nor possess it further—for they have been rejected by God forever—and the ten tribes are no more to return to the land of their fathers (as has been shown through the aforementioned tradition), therefore whatever is read in *Ezekiel* or elsewhere concerning *Gog and Magog* must be understood not literally, but spiritually. Indeed, this can be shown from the fact that in the aforementioned chapter *Helec*, it is read thus: *Rabbi Abba said*, "The house which is before God, the holy and blessed one, is eighteen thousand leagues." Just as it is said at the end of *Ezekiel*: *It was eighteen thousand round about.* <note>original Hebrew: סביב שמונה עשר אלף ; see Ezekiel 48:35.</note> Where the gloss of *Rabbi Solomon* <note>Rashi</note> says: "The scriptures at the end of Ezekiel spoke concerning the heavenly *Jerusalem*." Likewise in *Midrash Koheleth* <note>A rabbinic commentary (Midrash) on the Book of Ecclesiastes.</note>, in the exposition of the book of *Ecclesiastes* upon that saying in chapter 10, *Who is as the wise man?*, it is said thus: "This is the first *Adam*, of whom it was said in *Ezekiel 28*: *Son of Adam, raise a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and say to him, Thus says the Lord God: You were the seal, or the ring of resemblance, full of wisdom.*" <note>original Hebrew: בן אדם שא קינה על מלך צור ואמרת לו כה אמר אדני יהוה אתה חותם תכנית מלא חכמה ; see Ezekiel 28:12.</note> 

Also in the book *Bava Batra* <note>A tractate of the Talmud dealing with civil law and property.</note>, in the chapter *Hammocher eth hassephina* <note>Literally "The one who sells the ship," the fifth chapter of Bava Batra.</note>, it is read thus: *Rabbi Hanina said*, "The holy and blessed God made ten coverings for the first *Adam* in the garden of pleasure." Just as it is said (namely, in the same place in *Ezekiel* immediately following): *You have been in the delights of the garden of God; every precious stone was your covering: the sardius, the topaz, and the diamond, the chrysolite, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the carbuncle, and the emerald, and gold; the workmanship of your timbrels and of your pipes was prepared in you in the day that you were created.* <note>original Hebrew: בעדן גן אלהים היית כל אבן משכתך אדם פטרה ויהלם תרשיש שהם וישפה ספיר נפך וברקת וזהב מלאכת תפיך ונקביך בך ביום הבראך כוננו ; see Ezekiel 28:13.</note> That is: *In the delights of the garden of God you have been; every precious stone was your covering:*

Sardius, topaz, chrysolite, onyx, jasper, sapphire, beryl, carbuncle, emerald, and gold: these were the workmanship of your timbrels <note>original Latin: "tympani"; likely referring to the musical instruments or the settings for the gems</note>. In which, even if this idea—that God wished to make Hezekiah the Messiah and Sennacherib into Gog and Magog—is legendary unless understood spiritually, we nevertheless have our point regarding *Gog* and *Magog*: that they ought to be understood mystically.

<margin>How Gog and Magog are interpreted.</margin>

> <term>טוב שבת על פנת גג מאשת מדיונים ובית חבר</term> <note>original Hebrew: "Tov shevet al pinnat gag me-eshet midyanim u-veit chaver"</note> That is: It is better to sit in a corner of the roof than with a quarrelsome woman in a shared house.

And from this comes <term>מגג Magog</term>, which is the same as "from the roof." For this reason, the devil is rightly called Magog, as he proceeds from the house. Furthermore, Gog will especially be the Antichrist in the final times; he will be the roof and the house of the devil, from whom Magog—that is, the devil—will emerge through open persecution. And for that reason, it was said to Gog himself in Ezekiel:

### *Regarding the twelfth Jewish objection: That Jesus the Nazarene was not the true Messiah because he left no seed behind him, nor did he have sons. Chapter XIII.*

## CAPNIO, <note>The pseudonym of the famous Christian Hebraist Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a character in this dialogue.</note>

Notwithstanding these things, the Jewish unbelief <term>perfidia</term> <note>In this period, 'perfidia' was a standard polemical term for the refusal to accept Christian doctrine.</note>, wishing to show that our Lord Jesus Christ was not the true Messiah, finally opposes us with that which is said concerning the Messiah in the fifty-third chapter of Isaiah:
> <term>יראה זרע יאריך ימים וחפץ יהוה בידו יצלח</term> <note>original Hebrew: "yir’eh zerah yaarikh yamim ve-chephetz YHWH be-yado yitzlach"</note> This means: He shall see a long-lived seed, and the will of God shall prosper in his hand.

And also that which is written in the eighty-eighth Psalm <note>Psalm 89 in modern Bibles.</note> concerning the same:
> <term>ושמתי לעד זרעו וכסאו כימי שמים</term> <note>original Hebrew: "ve-samti la-ad zar’o ve-khis’o ki-yemei shamayim"</note> That is: And I will establish his seed forever, and his throne as the days of heaven.

Therefore (they say), since your Jesus had no sons, nor left behind the seed of sons after him, he could not possibly be the Messiah. **GAL.** <note>Pietro Galatino (c. 1460–1540), the author of this work and a character in the dialogue.</note> Their madness in this matter can easily be refuted if even one of the things I say is committed to memory. For it is read thus in the <term>Bereshit Rabbah Minor</term> <note>A collection of Jewish midrashic (interpretive) teachings on the Book of Genesis.</note> regarding that which is said in the twenty-fifth chapter of Genesis:
> <term>ויוסף אברהם ויקח אשה ושמה קטורה</term> <note>original Hebrew: "Va-yoseph Avraham va-yikkach ishah u-shemah Keturah"</note> That is: And Abraham added, and took a wife, and her name was Keturah.

It is written in the 11th chapter of Ecclesiastes: <term>בבקר זרע</term> <note>original Hebrew: "ba-boker zera," meaning "In the morning [sow your] seed."</note>

<meta>This page transitions from the metaphorical interpretation of Gog and Magog to a broader discussion on the biblical and rabbinical definitions of "seed" and "sonship." ### FIFTH BOOK

**In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not let your hand rest.** <note>original Hebrew: *et zarchakha u-la-erev al tanach yadekha*, from Ecclesiastes 11:6</note> That is: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not let your hand cease in the evening. For you do not know which will be more suitable or right—whether this one or that one, or if both alike are good. Rabbi Akiba <note>A leading Jewish scholar and sage of the late 1st and early 2nd centuries.</note> says: If you have had disciples in your youth, instruct disciples also in your old age. For you do not know which of them God will assign to you, or whether all will be good together. So it is said there. Since in this context, disciples taught by someone are called his "seed," the apostles and his other disciples were therefore the seed of Christ. In the *Bereshith Rabba* <note>The "Great Genesis," a collection of ancient Jewish explanations and stories about the Book of Genesis.</note> as well, regarding that passage in Genesis chapter 28, "To you I will give it and to your seed," it is said: "Your seed shall be like you." Just as it is said in Deuteronomy chapter 23: "And Israel shall dwell in confidence, the eye of Jacob alone." And regarding this, the prophet Amos asked for mercy, saying in chapter 7: "Lord God, spare, I pray, or spare now. Who shall raise up Jacob?"—that is, *like* Jacob. Although he himself is small (or "is he not small?"), He had mercy regarding this. And so on. This is the tradition, where it must be noted that those like Jacob are called his "seed."

It is also read in this way in the **Massekhet Bikkurim** <note>The "Tractate of First Fruits," part of the Mishnah dealing with offerings brought to the Temple.</note>, that is, in the book of first fruits. They handed down in the name of Rabbi Judah that a **proselyte** <term>gher</term>—that is, a convert who has come from the pagans to the faith—personally brings the first fruits and learns (or recites) that passage from Deuteronomy chapter 26: "I declare today to the Lord your God that I have entered the land which God swore to your fathers." What is the proof for this? It is what was said in Genesis chapter 17: **"No longer shall your name be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham."** <margin>Why Abram was called Abraham.</margin> This means: Your name shall no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, because I have made you a father of a multitude of nations. For in the beginning, he was the "Father of Aram" <note>Aram being a region in the ancient Near East; "Ab-Ram" is interpreted here as "Father of Aram."</note>, and so he was called Abram. But finally, he became the father of the whole world, and for that reason, he was called Abraham. This is the tradition.

In the book *Sanhedrin*, in the chapter **Judgments of Wealth** <margin>mamonot</margin> <term>Dine mamonoth</term> <note>A section of the Talmud dealing with civil laws and monetary disputes.</note>, it is said: It is written in Genesis chapter 49, "The scepter shall not depart from Judah." These are the ones who were the heads of the Babylonian exiles, who ruled Israel with a scepter. "And a scribe from between his feet." These are the sons of the sons of Hillel <note>Hillel the Elder was a famous Jewish leader whose descendants led the Jewish community for generations.</note>, teaching the law to Israel. So it is said there. Therefore, the masters taught by Hillel were called his "sons." For among the Hebrews, everyone is called the son of the one by whom he was taught or nourished. 

For this reason, in the same book, in the chapter **High Priest** <term>cohen gadol</term>, it is read: It is written in the twenty-first chapter of the Second Book of Kings <note>Known in modern Bibles as 2 Samuel 21:8.</note>, "And the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul." Rabbi Joshua said: Merab gave birth to them, but Michal raised them, though she never had children of her own. For as it is written in the sixth chapter of the Second Book of Kings <note>2 Samuel 6:23.</note>, no son was born to Michal the daughter of Saul until the day of her death. Therefore, because she raised them, they were called her sons. This is to teach you the scripture: that whoever raises an orphan or a fatherless child in the middle of their house is considered their father, just as if he had begotten him. Rabbi Johanan said: Whoever teaches the son of his neighbor, the scripture regards him no differently than if he had begotten him. Just as it is said...

<summary>This page explores the rabbinical and biblical definitions of "seed" and "sonship," arguing that teaching and raising children—even if not biologically one's own—establishes a parental bond recognized by scripture. These precedents are used to explain how the Apostles are the "seed" of Christ and how Abraham became the "father of all nations."</summary>

# BOOK V.

...is found in Numbers, chapter 3: "And these are the generations of Aaron and Moses." <note>original Hebrew: *ve-eleh toldot Aharon u-Moshe*</note> Then it follows: "And these are the names of the sons of Aaron." <note>original Hebrew: *ve-eleh shemot bene Aharon*</note> But Aaron indeed fathered them, while Moses taught them. And for that reason, they are called his sons, just as they are called Aaron's. All of this is from the Talmud. <note>Specifically referring to Sanhedrin 19b, which states that whoever teaches the son of his neighbor the Torah, the Scripture ascribes it to him as if he had begotten him.</note> From all these things, therefore, it is clear that even if our Lord Jesus did not have biological children, he nevertheless had infinite spiritual children. For not only the apostles and his other disciples taught directly by him are called his sons, but also all the rest of the Christians who follow and observe his teaching. Therefore, the "long-lived seed" which he left behind is not physical, but spiritual. This was not done without a hidden meaning. For just as he himself descended from a seed that was not physical but spiritual, so too must he have a seed that is not physical but spiritual. 

That the Messiah was to come from a spiritual seed is evident from the promise made to Abraham concerning the Messiah himself, when God said to him in Genesis chapter 22: "And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed." <note>original Hebrew: *ve-hitbarakhu ve-zar'akha kol goye ha-aretz*</note> And in a preceding chapter, it is said that the Lord told him: "For through Isaac your seed shall be named." <note>original Hebrew: *ki ve-Yitzchak yikare lekha zara* (Genesis 21:12)</note> And yet it is well known that Isaac was conceived according to the spirit, and not according to the flesh like Ishmael. As the Apostle says when writing to the Galatians <note>Referring to Galatians 4:22-31, where Paul allegorizes the two sons of Abraham.</note>. All the more so, then, and much more greatly should the Messiah—who was to be conceived not from human seed but from a mystical breath (as will be proven most extensively in what follows)—be said to be conceived according to the spirit. Therefore, because Jesus of Nazareth, the true Messiah, was born entirely according to the spirit from a virgin without a man, he was destined to have spiritual rather than biological children.

<margin>Two ages.</margin>
This is also clearly shown from the Hebrew commentary on the phrase, "In Isaac your seed shall be named," which says that two ages are noted there: one of the Law, and the other of the Messiah. In the age of the Law, there were physical seed and children. But in the age of the Messiah, the seed and children were to be spiritual, just as Isaac was born according to the spirit. And David spoke of children of this kind in Psalm 45, which according to the ancient Hebrew scholars is interpreted as being about the Messiah, saying: "In place of your fathers, sons have been born to you." <note>original Hebrew: *tachat avotekha yihyu vanekha* (Psalm 45:16)</note>

# Book Six.

## Concerning the redemption and salvation of the human race, for which the Messiah was to come and which could not be accomplished except by God and man.

*That there was to be no savior and redeemer except God, who was to give himself as the price of human redemption. Chapter 1.*

->CAPNIO,<-
<note>Capnio is the scholar’s pseudonym for Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous German humanist and student of Hebrew.</note>

Most excellently and quite abundantly indeed, my Galatinus, you have proven in the preceding parts—through the authentic scriptures of the ancient Jews—that not only has the fixed time of the Messiah’s first coming already passed, but also that the Messiah himself has already come, and that this same Messiah was none other than our Lord Jesus. Therefore, so that the impiety of the Jews of our age may be more thoroughly exposed, we must now speak of the redemption and salvation of the human race, for which the Messiah himself was to come, and which could only be accomplished through a God-man. For this reason, in order to proceed in an orderly fashion, it must first be shown that there was to be no savior and redeemer except God, who would give himself as the price of human redemption.

The Holy One, blessed be He, said to David: "David, with what confidence <note>original Hebrew: *torpusia*, a loanword from Greek *parrhesia*, meaning boldness or freedom of speech</note> do you say these words?" He said to Him: "Because I trust in Your mercy, as it is said, 'But I have trusted in Your mercy' [Psalm 13:6]; in that same mercy about which it is said, 'The earth is full of the mercy of the Lord' [Psalm 33:5]." And it says, "If I said, 'My foot slips,' Your mercy, O Lord, held me up" [Psalm 94:18]. Another interpretation: "But I have trusted in Your mercy"—this refers to the Law, the chosen one, the feared one. It says, "And the law of kindness is on her tongue" [Proverbs 31:26]. "My heart shall rejoice in Your salvation" [Psalm 13:6]. This is one of the difficult scriptures, for the salvation of the Holy One, blessed be He, is the salvation of Israel. It is not written here as "our salvation," but "Your salvation." David said: "Our salvation is Your salvation."

That is, the Holy and Blessed God said to David: "David, how do you presume to say words of this kind?" He said to him, "Because I have trusted in your mercy." Just as it is said, **But I have trusted in your mercy.** Specifically in that mercy of which it is said, **The earth is full of the mercy of God.** Of which it is also said, **If I said, "My foot is moved," your mercy, O God, shall sustain me.** Another discourse: **And I have trusted in your mercy,** namely in the Law, as it is said, **And the law of piety is on her tongue.** **My heart shall exult in your salvation.** This is one of the hardest scriptures: Namely, that the salvation of the Holy and Blessed God is the salvation of Israel. "Our salvation" is not written in this way, but "Your salvation." Therefore David said: "Our salvation, that itself is your salvation." These things are found there. From which it is openly gathered that God himself was going to be the savior of Israel. Who, once Israel itself was saved, would be said to have saved himself, because of the <note>This is the core of Galatino's argument: God "saves himself" by taking on a human body and redeeming it.</note> assumption of our nature. **The LORD.** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה (YHWH)</note> This is: **Blessed are you, O Israel. Who is like you, a people saved** in God, or through God, or with God? It is not written, "A people whom God will save," but rather **a people saved in God.** <note>The author is highlighting a grammatical distinction in Deuteronomy 33:29, arguing that the people are "saved in" God's very being rather than just "by" His actions.</note> This is like a certain man who has a small measure of wheat from the second tithe. <note>The "second tithe" (Maaser Sheni) was a portion of produce that, according to Jewish law, had to be eaten in Jerusalem or redeemed for money to be spent there.</note> What does he do? As it is said in the **thirty-third chapter of Deuteronomy: A people saved in God, or through God, or with God.** For God said: In this world, you were saved through the hands of the sons of Adam. In the days of *Sisera*, <note>A Canaanite general; his defeat is recounted in the book of Judges.</note> it was through the hands of *Barack* and *Deborah*. Thus far the tradition. In which six truly wonderful things are expressed, which are very much in agreement with our faith. The first is when it says, *He who sacrifices a confession shall see the salvation of God.* <note>The author is likely referring to Psalm 50:23. In Latin, "confessio" can mean both a confession of sin and a confession of praise/faith.</note> The second is that God said He would be with man in tribulation. The fourth is that then God Himself would be saved, and he shows through the authorities he brings forward that this would happen in the *Messiah*. And therefore, it follows that God was to be saved in the *Messiah*. For this reason, it did not seem out of place to many of the ancient wise men of the Hebrews—though it seemed very difficult to accept—that in the aforementioned authorities, God is called not the "Savior of Israel," but the "one saved." <note>This refers to a mystical and linguistic interpretation of Hebrew grammar where God is described as being "saved" alongside His people, implying His deep participation in the human condition.</note> The fifth is that through the comparison provided, God was to be the price of human redemption. The sixth and finally, that it was to happen that God, in His own substance, would save Israel. For that itself is our salvation.
