This means: And he shall be for a sanctification or preparation, and for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of scandal to the two houses of Israel, and for a snare and for ruin to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And many of them shall stumble, and fall, and be bound, and be ensnared, and be captured. Bind the testimony, and seal the law in my disciples. And I will wait for God, hiding his faces from the house of Jacob, and I will wait for him. The Rabbi said to them: "My sons, you are thrusting thorns into my eyes." Rabbi Hiyya said to him: "Rabbi, let this not be an evil thing to you. Wine was given in 70, and the secret was given in 70. Wine entered, and the secret came out." <note>This refers to the practice of Gematria, where letters have numerical values. Both the Hebrew word for "wine" (Yayin) and "secret" (Sod) equal 70, suggesting that wine reveals hidden truths.</note> This is the tradition. Moreover, Rabbi Kimhi <note>David Kimhi (Radak), a famous 12th-13th century Jewish commentator.</note> in explaining that passage of Isaiah, **And he shall be for a sanctification**, says: "This means, he will be a place to which a man goes so that he may be saved in it." There are also those who explain: **He shall be for a sanctification**, that is, for a "preparation"—as if he were saying, for the preparation of vengeance, according to what is said in Jeremiah chapter 12: **Sanctify them for the day of slaughter.** <note>original: "והקדישם ליום הרגה" (ve-hikdisham le-yom haregah).</note> Thus says Rabbi Kimhi. 

Concerning this tradition, therefore, it must first be noted that those words of Isaiah, **And he shall be for a sanctification**, along with the rest, are spoken concerning the Messiah. Secondly, for the truth of this matter and the meaning of the verse that precedes these words—namely, **Sanctify the Lord of Hosts himself** <note>original: "את יהוה צבאות אותו תקדישו"</note>—the Chaldaic translation <note>The Targum, an Aramaic paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible.</note> of Rabbi Jonathan says: **And let him be your fear, and let him be your strengthener. And he shall be for a sanctification**, and so forth. From which it follows necessarily that the Messiah is not only man, but also God. Thirdly, it must also be noted that the Messiah was intended to be a "sanctification and preparation" not for all, but for some from among the Jews—that is, only those who believe in him and obey him—so that he might make them holy and prepared...

...would lead to the reception of the glory of eternal life. For the unbelievers, however, who were to be much more numerous, it was bound to lead to manifold destruction and perdition (their own treachery demanding it). This is noted when it says, *And many of them shall stumble*, along with the other things that follow. <note>The author is citing Isaiah 8:15 to argue that the Messiah would be a "stone of stumbling" for many in Israel.</note> And for this reason specifically, this Talmudic tradition was introduced in this place. 

Fourth, it must also be observed that God was destined to reject all the Jews who would not believe in the Messiah, and to take away from them the grace of understanding the Scriptures, bestowing it instead upon the disciples of the Messiah. All of this is suggested when it is said: *Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. And I will wait for God, who hides his face from the house of Jacob* <note>Isaiah 8:16-17</note>—that is, from the Jews. 

Fifth, it must also be noted that this tradition was held in the highest regard among the ancient fathers because of the great mysteries it contained regarding the Messiah, and it was kept secret. 

Sixth, that no secret remains hidden where the power of wine prevails. <note>A reference to the anecdote on the previous page where wine loosened the tongues of scholars to reveal messianic secrets.</note> 

Seventh, finally, that the Messiah was to come after the destruction of the heads of the Babylonian captivity—namely Zerubbabel and his sons—and Mattathias and his family, that is, the Maccabees, whom they call the <term>Hashmonai</term> <note>original: "חשמונאי" (Hashmonai), the Hasmonean dynasty.</note>. The <term>Yavan</term> <note>original: "יון" (Yavan), meaning the Greeks.</note>, that is, the Greeks, deposed the sons of Zerubbabel and utterly took away the dominion of the Jews from them. This can be seen most clearly from the fact that Mattathias and his sons later forcefully extorted that same dominion from the hands of the Greeks and became the Princes of the Jews, until Herod the Ascalonite, who later rose up against them and seized the kingdom from their hands, as we have discussed more extensively elsewhere. 

And so, according to the aforementioned tradition, the two houses of the fathers of Israel ceased, which were the heads of the captivity that had returned from Babylon—namely, Zerubbabel and his kin, and the princes who were in the land of Israel, who were the Maccabees. Therefore, after the destruction of the Maccabees in the time of Herod the Ascalonite (who destroyed the Maccabees), it is certain according to this Talmudic tradition that the Messiah came, and that the Jews were for the most part destroyed shortly thereafter. 

That only a few of the Jews were to be saved—excepting those who, being converted near the end of the world, will perform penance for their sin—is evident from what Isaiah testified in chapter 10, saying: <term>For though your people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return</term> <note>original: "כי אם יהיה עמך ישראל כחול הים שאר ישוב בו"</note>. Rabbi Jonathan translated this into Aramaic as follows: <term>For if your people Israel be as numerous as the sand of the sea, a remnant who have not sinned, or who have repented of sin, shall return</term> <note>original: "ארי אם יהי עמך ישראל סגי כחלא דימא שאר דלא חטו ויתחבו יתובון מחתאת" — this refers to the Targum Jonathan, an ancient Aramaic translation and commentary.</note>. 

Furthermore, the gloss of <term>Rabbi Solomon</term> <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator on the Bible and Talmud.</note> on the aforementioned words of Isaiah says: "Even if Israel should be like the sand of the sea in its multitude, I will refine them like silver, and they shall be reduced to a small number; but the remnant of that small number shall be turned toward good." 

To these things it must also be added that in the book of the <term>Sanhedrin</term>, in the chapter <term>Helek</term> <note>Chapter "Helek" (The Portion) is famous for its discussions on the World to Come and the arrival of the Messiah.</note>, it is written thus: "John said: In the generation in which the son of David is to come, the wise teachers will be diminished. The eyes of the rest will fail in grief and sighing. Many troubles and harsh decrees will be renewed against them; for before the first has been carried out, the second will already arrive." From all of these points, our proposition is clear.

### *That the Jews who were not going to receive the Messiah were bound to lose the understanding of the Scriptures, remaining as fools and asses without sense.*

->Chapter III.<-

**CAPNIO,** <note>Capnio is the Latinized name of Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous Christian Hebraist who appears as a character in this dialogue.</note>

**I** would like you to show from their own writings that which you have already said in the preceding remarks: namely, that the grace of understanding the Scripture was to be taken away from the Jews and conferred upon the disciples of the Messiah. And especially, I would like you to show that those who would not receive the Messiah were destined to utterly lose the understanding of the Scriptures. **GALATINUS.** First, this is clearly contained in the book of the *Sanhedrin* <note>The Sanhedrin is a tractate of the Talmud dealing with the high court and messianic prophecies.</note>, in the chapter *Helec*, where it reads as follows: Rabbi Judas said, "In the generation in which the son of David <note>A common title for the Messiah.</note> is to come, the house of preaching will be for fornication." <gloss>Gloss of Rabbi Solomon: that is, the place where the wise masters taught the law.</gloss> <note>Rabbi Solomon refers to Rashi, the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator.</note> "And the men of Gazith" <gloss>Gloss of Rabbi Solomon: that is, the Sanhedrin, which is the 70 ordinary Judges.</gloss> "will wander from city to city, and no one will have mercy on them. And the wisdom of the scribes will stink, and those who fear to sin will be rejected. And the face of that generation will be like a dog" <gloss>Gloss of Rabbi Solomon: literally, they will be as shameless as dogs.</gloss> "and truth will be diminished." Also in the book *Siphre* <note>An ancient Jewish commentary (Midrash) on Numbers and Deuteronomy.</note>, that saying of Deuteronomy chapter 32 is explained thus: *A crooked and perverse generation, do you thus requite the Lord, O foolish and unwise people?* <note>original: "דור עקש ופתלתל הל יהוה תגמלו זאת עם נבל ולא חכם"</note> "O foolish people," namely in those things which have gone before; "and not wise," specifically in those things which will happen in the world to come. And this is what was said in Isaiah chapter 1: *Israel has not known, my people have not understood.* <note>original: "ישראל לא ידע עמי לא התבונן"</note> Israel has not known those things which have passed; my people have not understood regarding the world to come. What did Israel do to deserve to be infatuated and hardened in heart? Because they did not act wisely regarding the words of the law. And so Job himself says in chapter 4: *Has not their cord departed with them? They shall die, and not in knowledge or wisdom.* <note>original: "הלא נסע יתרם בס ימותו ולא בחכמה"</note> Thus far the tradition. Therefore, since the "world to come" or the "future world" in the Talmud almost always refers to the time of the Messiah, it is quite clearly held according to the aforementioned tradition that the Jews were infatuated for this reason: because they were not wise, nor did they understand the words of the law in which the Messiah is evidently shown, so that they might receive him. Their "cord" then departed from them when, denying the Messiah—God their Savior—they fell headlong into the whirlpool of the Roman Empire in this world, and into the pit of hell in the future world. They are like one who lets himself down from a height by a rope, which, once snapped, causes him to fall headlong into the abyss. This is according to that prophecy of Isaiah in the 5th chapter: *Therefore my people are led away captive, because they were without knowledge, and their honorable men have died of hunger, and their common people are parched with thirst. Therefore hell has enlarged its soul, and opened its mouth without limit; and their glory, and their multitude, and their loftiness, and he that rejoices in it, shall descend into it.* <note>original: "לכן גלה עמי מבלי דעת וכבודו מתי רעב והמונו צמא צמא : לכן הרחיבה שאול נפשה ופערה פיה לבלי חק וירד הדרה והמונה ושאונה ועלז בה"</note> This means: Because of this my people were taken captive, because they were without knowledge...

<summary>Galatinus argues that Jewish tradition and scripture predicted the Jewish people would lose their spiritual wisdom and understanding as a consequence of rejecting the Messiah. He cites the Talmud and various biblical prophets to illustrate this spiritual blindness and its subsequent historical consequences, such as the Roman conquest.</summary>

...[Hell] has enlarged its soul <note>original: *dilatauit infernus animam suam*</note>, and opened its mouth without limit. And his nobility shall descend, and his common people, and his noise. And hell, namely, shall rejoice in him. Moreover, upon these words, *Hell has enlarged its soul*, along with the rest, the gloss of **Rabbi Rahmo** <note>Likely a reference to a specific Rabbinic commentator cited in polemical works.</note> says: **Measure for measure.** For they themselves enlarged themselves to swallow too much food and drink, and they opened their mouths to deny God their savior, just as it is said in Jeremiah, chapter 5: **They have denied God, and said, "He is not he."** <note>original: *Negauerunt Deum, & dixerunt non est ipse*</note>

Also in the book **Haghiga** <note>The Talmudic tractate *Chagigah*, which deals with festival offerings and also contains mystical and ethical teachings.</note>, that is, *Of the Festival*, in the chapter that begins, **Haccol hayabin**, that is, *All are bound*, it is read in this way: It is written in Jeremiah, chapter 49: **Counsel has perished from the sons, and their wisdom has become foul.** <note>original: אבדה עצה מבנים נסרחה חכמתם</note> When was counsel lost from the sons and their wisdom made foul? When they were among the nations of the world. For the devil (with God’s permission) infatuated the Jews and took from them the sense for understanding the truth. And indeed, it has reached such a point that they have less understanding of the divine scriptures than asses. This is something they themselves are forced to admit. For in the book **Sekalim** <note>The tractate *Shekalim*, concerning the half-shekel temple tax.</note>, that is, *Of the Weights*, in the chapter that begins **Ve ellu hen**, that is, *And these are they*, it is read thus word for word:

> **Rabbi Haggai said**, "The earlier generations plowed, and sowed, and hoed, and reaped, and gathered into barns, and threshed, and winnowed, and ground the grain, and set the bread before us"—that is, the doctrine of Scripture—"and we do not have a mouth to eat it." **Rabbi Abba said**, "If the ancients were sons of men, we are asses." **Rabbi Men said** at that hour, "We are not even to be compared to the female asses of **Rabbi Pinhas son of Yair**." <note>A reference to a famous Talmudic story where Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair's donkey was so pious it refused to eat grain that had not been properly tithed.</note>

All these things are in the Talmud. Yet another testimony concerning this is held in the book **Sabbath** <note>The tractate *Shabbat*, dealing with the laws of the Sabbath.</note>, that is, *Of the Sabbath*, where it is said literally:

> **Rabbi Zera said**, because Rabbi [Judah] said: "If the earlier ones were sons of men, we are asses. And we are not even like the donkey of **Rabbi Hanina** or like the donkey of **Rabbi Menahem**, but like other common asses."

From these things, although all Jews who have not received Christ are proven to be asses, it is established that those who draw others into the pit with false dogma are even worse than asses. Jeremiah calls these people "shepherds," and calls their behavior "bestiality," saying in chapter 10: **Because the shepherds have become like beasts, and have not sought God: therefore they have not understood, and all their flock is scattered.** <note>original: כי נבערו הרועים ואת יהוה לא דרשו : על כן לא השכילו וכל מרעיתם נפוצה</note> Again, in chapter 50, he says: **Lost sheep have my people been, their shepherds have made them go astray.** Certainly, the shepherds of the Jews—namely their masters and doctors—even if they made them go astray many times in the past, they make them go astray most of all today. Therefore, the Savior, speaking of them in the 15th chapter of Matthew, did not speak inaptly when he said: **They are blind, and leaders of the blind. If the blind lead the blind, both fall into the pit.**

# *On the perpetual rejection of the Jews, and that they were to be expelled from the house of God as enemies of God. Chapter IV.*

## CAPNIO,

Since God has cast the Jews out of his house as rebels and enemies against him, and has rejected them forever, testimonies must be brought forward from their own scriptures to show that these things were to happen to them for their confusion. G A L. These things are evident especially by the testimony of Hosea; thus in chapter 9, in the person of God speaking: **Because of the wickedness of their deeds, I will drive them out of my house; I will love them no more.** <note>original Hebrew: על רע מעלליהם מבית אגרשם לא אוסיף אהבתם</note> This is to say: Because of the malice of their works, I will expel them from my house, nor will I continue to love them. Which Rabbi Jonathan <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, the traditional author of the Aramaic Targum of the Prophets.</note> thus interpreted in Chaldean <term>Chaldean: An early modern term for Aramaic</term>: **Because of the malice of their works, I will expel them from my holy house, nor will I add to have mercy upon them.** <note>original Aramaic: על בישת עובדיהון מבית מקדשי אתרכינון לא אוסיף לרחמא עליהון</note> Regarding this, the prophet **Amos** also says in chapter 5: **The virgin of Israel has fallen, she shall rise no more.** <note>original Hebrew: נפלה לא תוסיף קום בתולת ישראל</note> That is: She has fallen, and she will not add to her rising, the virgin of Israel.
<margin>Objection of the Jews.</margin>

<margin>Response.</margin>
G A L. This was more expressly foretold in Jeremiah chapter 7, speaking thus: **And I will cast you out from my presence, just as I cast out all your brothers, all the seed of Ephraim.** <note>original Hebrew: והשלכתי אתכם מעל פני באשר השלכתי את כל אחיכם את כל זרע אפרים</note> That is: I will expel you from my face, just as I expelled all your brothers, all the seed of Ephraim. Thus it is said: In the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, performs mercy with Judah, it is the same as if he himself performs mercy with the whole of Israel. For all of Israel is called by the name of Judah. For Israel is called by four names, namely Jacob, Israel, Ephraim, and Judah. Concerning this rejection, **Amos** himself also said in chapter 6: **The Lord God has sworn by his soul, says the Lord God of hosts: I detest the pride of Jacob, and I hate his palaces, and I have delivered up the city and its fullness.** <note>original Hebrew: נשבע אדני יהוה בנפשו נאם יהוה אלהי צבאות מתאב אנכי את גאון יעקב וארמנותיו שנאתי והסגרתי עיר ומלאה</note> That is: The Lord God swore by his soul. The Lord God of hosts said: I loathe the house of the sanctuary, which is the pride of the house of Jacob. Furthermore, the Gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki), the preeminent medieval commentator.</note> says: *I have delivered up the city and its fullness*—that is, Jerusalem and its inhabitants. Also, the house of the sanctuary was called "pride," according to that which was said in Ezekiel chapter 24: **Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength.** <note>original Hebrew: הנני מחלל את מקדשי גאון עוזכם</note> That is: Behold, I pro—

...I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength. <note>original: "phanabo fanctuarium meum, elationem fortitudinis ueftræ." A reference to Ezekiel 24:21.</note> Thus says Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Solomon: Referring to Rashi (Solomon ben Isaac), the preeminent medieval French rabbi and commentator.</note>.

C A P N I O. Why is this rejection of the Jews so often called "contrition" <term>contrition: From the Latin "contritio," meaning a literal breaking or grinding into pieces, as well as spiritual remorse.</term> in the sacred scriptures, which is not ineptly compared to a shattered potter's flask?
<margin>Why the rejection of the Jews is called contrition.</margin>
G A L A T I N U S. Because the pressure upon them in this captivity was to be so great that it could deservedly be compared to a crushing from which not even the smallest shard remains. For every break in a vessel can be soldered and restored to some useful work. But the shards of a flask, if they are broken by a violent crushing, their parts are good for nothing except to be cast away. And the more a shattered shard lasts, the more its fracture is always increased. Therefore, since their rejection is compared to the crushing of such shards, which are worth nothing further except to be thrown outside, it is openly given to be understood that they were to fall into such great dejection in this captivity that, as long as they remain in their perfidy <note>perfidy: Used here in the historical sense of "unbelief" or "faithlessness" regarding Christian doctrine.</note>, they can never return to their former liberty. According to that saying of the Psalmist in Psalm 2:
<margin>Psalm 2.</margin>
**You shall break them with a rod of iron; you shall dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.** <note>original Hebrew: תרועם בשבט ברזל ככלי יוצר תנפצם (Psalm 2:9)</note>
And you shall cast them away like a potter's vessel. From these things which have been said, therefore, it is manifest: the Jews, because of the malice of their works, were deservedly to be cast out from the house of God by God himself, and never to be loved by him as long as they would persist in the malice of their perfidy. Foreseeing this, Jeremiah, at the end of his Lamentations, sought the cause, saying:
**Why do you forget us forever, and forsake us for so long a time? Turn us to yourself, Lord, etc.** <note>original Hebrew: למה לנצח תשכחנו השיבנו אליך וגו' לאורך ימים (Lamentations 5:20-21)</note>
That is: Why do you forget us for eternity, and leave us for the length of days? To which the Lord replied in the 8th chapter of the same prophet, saying thus:
**And you shall say to them, Thus says the Lord: Shall they fall and not rise? Shall he turn away and not return? Why then has this people of Jerusalem turned back with a perpetual backsliding? They hold fast to deceit, they refuse to return. I listened and heard, but they do not speak what is right; no man repented of his wickedness, saying, "What have I done?" Everyone turned to his own course, like a horse rushing into battle. Even the stork in the heavens knows her appointed times, and the turtledove, the crane, and the swallow observe the time of their coming. But my people do not know the judgment of the Lord.** <note>original Hebrew: Jeremiah 8:4-7. The Latin text provides a translation followed by the Hebrew source.</note>
From these things, the point is clear.

...that they not only recognize themselves as speakers of falsehoods in this matter, but also that they hope in vain, because they are never to return to their land, nor will they ever possess it; this must be proven by their own scriptures. **GAL.** This is best established by what is found among them in the book *Yebamot* <note>original: "Iebamoth," a tractate of the Talmud primarily concerning levirate marriage.</note>, that is, *The Book of Sisters-in-Law*, in the chapter that begins *Ha'aretz* <note>Hebrew: "The Land."</note>, that is, *The Land*. Rabbi Yohanan <note>A leading 3rd-century rabbi in the Land of Israel.</note> said: Who was the author of *Seder Olam*, that is, the book of the *Order of the World*? Rabbi Jose. This is the tradition. This same point is also held in the same book, *Seder Olam*, in this manner: It is written in Deuteronomy chapter 30: "And the Lord your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it." Could it be possible that there might be a third possession in the future? It teaches what must be said to this by that which says, "Which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it." For they were to have a first and a second possession, but a third possession shall not be for them. This is the tradition. Since, therefore, the Jews were to possess their former land only twice, as is clearly evident from these traditions, and since they have already possessed it twice in the past—for first they possessed it from the time of Joshua until the destruction of the first Temple, and second from the times of Zerubbabel and Ezra until the burning of the last Temple, or until the times of Hadrian Caesar <note>Publius Aelius Hadrianus, the Roman Emperor who suppressed the Bar Kokhba revolt in 135 CE, leading to the mass displacement of Jews from Judea.</note>, as is evident in many ways from their scriptures—and since they are by no means to possess it a third time (as the aforementioned traditions attest), they must necessarily concede that they will never possess their land again, and consequently will not return to it. Therefore, whatever they object against us regarding their return to Jerusalem, the rebuilding of the Temple, and a third possession of that land, is entirely false and completely inconsistent with their own ancient scriptures. Indeed, the third possession of their land, for which they wait in vain, was to be given to the Saracens <note>A term used by the author to refer to the Muslim populations occupying the Holy Land at the time of writing.</note> for a time as a reproach to them, according to the testimony of Ezekiel. For in the seventh chapter he says: <insert>And I will lead in the worst of the nations, and they shall possess their houses: and I will make the pride of the mighty to cease; and they shall possess their holy places.</insert> <note>original: "והבאתי רעי גוים וירשו את בתיהם גאון עזים ונחלו מקדשיהם"</note> That is: I will bring the evil of the nations—that is, the Saracens—and they shall possess their lands, and I will make the pride of the strong to cease, and they shall inherit their sanctuaries. And further down: <insert>And the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.</insert> <note>original: "ותורה תאבד מכהן ועצה מזקנים"</note> And this is because they were meant to be without sacrifice, without a Prince, and indeed without God (as their perfidy <term>perfidy: Used here in the historical sense of "unbelief" or "faithlessness" regarding Christian doctrine.</term> requires) until the end of the world.

## That the Jews were to be without a Prince, without sacrifice, and without God until the end of the world. Chapter VI.

### CAPNIO,

**I** would like you to show from their own scriptures what you said last: namely, that the Jews were to be without a Prince, without sacrifice, and without God until the end of the world. **GAL.** This is best proven by what is said in the third chapter of <margin>Hosea 3</margin> Hosea: **For many days the children of Israel shall dwell** <note>original: "כי ימים רבים ישבו בני ישראל"</note>. This means: For many days the children of Israel shall remain without a King, and without a Prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an altar, and without an ephod <note>A ceremonial garment worn by the High Priest, often used in divination.</note> (that is, without the priestly ornament) and without images. Now, Rabbi Jonathan <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, the traditional author of the Aramaic translation (Targum) of the Prophets.</note> translated these words into Aramaic as follows: **Because for many days the children of Israel shall dwell, in which they will not have a King from the house of David, nor one bearing power over Israel, nor an acceptable or pleasing sacrifice in Jerusalem, nor an altar in Samaria, nor an ephod announcing [the future].** <note>original Aramaic: "ארי יומין סגיאין יתבו בני ישראל לית מלכא מדבית דוד ולית דיעביד שולטן על ישראל ולית דדבח לרעא בירושלם ולית קמתא בשומרון ולית אפוד ומחוי"</note> Just as it is shown, therefore, that the Jews were not to have a King from the house of David, nor any Prince from among themselves, nor a sacrifice, nor an altar, along with the other things placed here—it is also proven that they would have neither a priest, nor a law, nor even the true God, by that which is written in the 15th chapter of the second book of Chronicles: **Many days for Israel shall be without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without the law.** <note>original: "ימים רבים לישראל ללא אלהי אמת וללא כהן מורה וללא תורה"</note> 

Where I have translated "without the God of truth," the Hebrews deceitfully interpret it as "without judges of truth," because **God of truth** <note>original: "אלהי אמת," Elohe emeth</note> is written there, which they claim is a term that can refer both to God and to judges. But it is seen most clearly that they interpret this poorly and falsely from this fact: although the name **Elohim** <note>A plural Hebrew noun for God, which can sometimes refer to human judges or "mighty ones."</note> is sometimes found to signify "judges" in the sacred scriptures, in its primary meaning, it signifies God in the plural on account of the Trinity of divine persons. For this reason, it must be said that it signifies God here rather than judges. This is especially true since the ancient Talmudists themselves accept it as referring to the true God in this passage. For in the book **Avoda Zara** <note>A tractate of the Talmud concerning "Foreign Worship" or idolatry.</note> (that is, *Foreign Service*), in the chapter that begins **Liphne edehen** <note>Hebrew: "Before their festivals."</note> (that is, *Before their feasts*), it is read word-for-word as follows: Rabbi Hanina said to Rabbi Elazar: "Blessed are you, who have exercised yourself in the law and in works of mercy. And woe to me, who have exercised myself in the law only." Because as Rabbi Hunna said: "Whoever studies or exercises himself in the law only is like one who has no God." Just as it is written in the fifteenth chapter of the second book of Chronicles: *For many days Israel was without the true God, and without a priest, and without the law.* And what does "without the law" mean? Rabbi Hunna said: "Anyone who studies in the law only, and [not] in works of mercy..."

## Chapter VII.

### CAPNIO,

**A**lthough you have proved sufficiently and abundantly in the preceding sections that few of the Jews were to be saved at the time of the Messiah, while the rest were to be lost and scattered; it is nevertheless clear that those who received our Redeemer as the true Messiah were both saved and called by the changed name <term>Christians</term> <note>original Hebrew: "משיחים" (Messihim), meaning 'anointed ones'.</note>. But those who refused to receive him were neither saved nor called by another name. For to denote their unbelief, they are called Jews to this day, and will be so called as long as they remain in that state. Therefore, to further demonstrate this very unbelief of theirs, you ought to prove through their own scriptures that this division into unbelieving Jews and true Christians was to occur at the time of the Messiah. **GAL.** Truly, just as a division continually flourished between Israel and Judah—with Israel, of course, worshipping two golden calves as gods—so also the division between Christians and Jews never ceases to exist, with those same Jews denying the truth of our Lord Jesus Christ and the Christian faith. On this account, it should be known that the schism of the ten tribes imposed this name upon the "Jews." For previously they were called Hebrews, or Israel, or Israelites. From the time, therefore, that people was divided into two Kingdoms, whoever had Kings from the lineage of Judah, or from the tribe of Judah, were called Jews. But the ten tribes, and whoever in Samaria took Jeroboam as their King, were called Israel. For them, Jeroboam their King [made] two golden...

From which it is clearly held both that the ten tribes were rejected, and the cause of that rejection. It is also read in the book of the Sanhedrin <note>A volume of the Talmud dealing with legal matters and the afterlife.</note>, in the chapter *Helec*, in this manner: The <term>Rabbanan</term> <note>Aramaic for "The Rabbis" or "Our Teachers."</note> (that is, the Teachers) handed down: "That the ten tribes have no portion in the world to come, nor are they ever to return." For just as this day goes and does not return, so they, going away, shall never be returning. These are the words of Rabbi Akiba. However, Rabbi Eliezer said: "Just as this day grows dark and then shines forth, so it is with them. For just as it shall grow dark for them, so there shall be those among them for whom it shall shine." Thus far the Talmud. This last word of Rabbi Eliezer was verified in the time of Christ and his disciples, when many Gentiles who had been of the ten tribes of Israel were illuminated by the light of the Christian faith. For they had all been made Gentiles (as the following tradition shows). It should also be noted that the <term>world to come</term> <note>original Latin: "seculum uenturum"</note>, or the future world, is almost always accepted in Hebrew scriptures <term>for the time of the Messiah</term>. Or affirmatively: "May I be a Jew if I have done this." <note>The author is describing a historical polemical claim that the name "Jew" became a byproduct of an oath or a term of self-deprecation in legal contexts.</note> And the Lord God shall slay them, as the prophet says, until the end of the world, as has been shown in the preceding pages and will be shown even more extensively in those to follow.

...struction <note>the text continues from the previous page: "[the de]struction"</note>, which was to be carried out by the Romans, and concerning the cause of that same destruction, as well as the malice of their remnants, it was foretold in **Jeremiah chapter 5** in these words: <note>original Hebrew: שוטטו בחוצות ירושלם... "Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem and see now, and know, and seek in her broad places, if you can find a man, if there is any that executes judgment, that seeks the truth; and I will pardon her. And though they say, 'The Lord lives,' surely they swear falsely. O Lord, are not your eyes upon the truth? You have stricken them, but they have not grieved; you have consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction. They have made their faces harder than a rock; they have refused to return."</note> 

That is: **"Go about the streets of Jerusalem, and see, I pray you, and know, and search in her squares, if you might find a man doing justice, seeking faith, and I will be merciful to her,"** namely Jerusalem. **"And though they say, 'As God lives,' nevertheless they will swear to a falsehood. O God, are your eyes not toward faith? You have struck them, and they did not grieve. You have consumed them, and they refused to accept discipline, or correction. They hardened their faces more than a rock, and they refused to be converted."** 

And a little lower it adds: <note>original Hebrew: עלו בשורותיה ושחתו... "Go up upon her walls, and destroy; but make not a full end: take away her branches: for they are not the Lord’s. For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me, says the Lord. They have belied the Lord, and said, 'It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine: and the prophets shall become wind, and the word is not in them: thus shall it be done unto them.'"</note>

That is: **"Go up onto her walls, and scatter them, but do not make a total end. Take away the shoots and branches, because they are not God’s. For by betrayal they have betrayed me, the house of Israel and the house of Judah," says God. They have denied God** <term>tetragrammaton<note>the holy four-letter name of God, YHWH, which the author notes is used here in the Hebrew text</note></term> **and said, "it is not he, nor will evil come upon us, and we shall not see the sword and famine. And the prophets will be as wind, or as spirit, and the word will not be in them. This shall happen to them."** 

That these things were foretold regarding the destruction of the Jews which was to happen by the Romans is clear through their own commentators. For it is read thus in *Bereshit Rabbah*, Great and Small <note>original: *Beressith rabba ueketanna*—referring to the major and minor Midrashic commentaries on the book of Genesis</note>, upon that which is said in the **18th chapter** of the same book: **"And he said,"** namely Abraham, **"I pray you, let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet this once. What if ten should be found there? And he said, I will not destroy it for the sake of those ten."** 

Why ten? Because there had already remained eight in the generation of the flood <note>referring to Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their wives</note>, and God did not suspend his sentence because of their merits. Another explanation: Why ten? Because he supposed <gloss>thought</gloss> ten were there, namely Lot, and his wife, and his four daughters, and his four sons-in-law. 

But Rabbi Iodan and Rabbi Hanina said: "It is said here 'ten,' but in Jerusalem, even one." This is what is written in **Jeremiah chapter 5**: **"Go around Jerusalem,"** and so forth. And thus it is said elsewhere: in **Ecclesiastes chapter 7**, namely: **"One by one, to find the sum,"** or the number. Rabbi Isaac said: "And up to what point is the finding of the number? Down to one." Thus far the tradition. 

Therefore, the argument must be made here as follows. If, in the destruction of the first temple, there were several righteous men who could be found in Jerusalem—for Baruch the son of Neriah was there, of whom it is said in **Jeremiah chapter 36**: **"And Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah. And Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord."** There was also Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian, who pulled Jeremiah out of the cistern where he was dying, when he had spoken to the King thus (as held in **Jeremiah 38**): **"My Lord the King, these men have done evil in all that they have done..."**

->LIBER<-

[They] acted <note>The Latin 'cerunt' completes 'fecerunt' (they did/acted) from the previous page.</note> against Jeremiah the prophet, whom they cast into a pit so that he might die. To whom, and because of that deed, the Lord said (as written in Jeremiah 39): **"I will surely deliver you, and you shall not fall by the sword, but your life shall be as a prize to you, because you have put your trust in me,"** says the Lord. There was also there the house or family of the Rechabites, of whom it is said in the same prophet: **"Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak to them."** And a little later: **"There shall not fail a man of Jonadab the son of Rechab to stand before me forever."** Furthermore, there was Jeremiah the prophet himself, and many other righteous and holy men who were carried away into the Babylonian captivity. 

If, therefore, there were so many righteous people in Jerusalem at the time of the destruction of the first Temple, it is clearly shown from the conclusion <term>conclusion (calce)</term> of the aforementioned tradition—which states that no righteous person was found in Jerusalem—that the beginning of Jeremiah’s words, when he says, **"Go about the streets of Jerusalem,"** and the rest, does not speak of the first destruction of that city, which was done by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, but of the final one, which happened under Vespasian and Titus, the Roman Princes.

The reason why God destroyed and rejected the Jews through the Romans is shown where it is said in the same place: **"For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me,"** said God. But what and of what kind this treachery was is clearly suggested when it immediately follows: **"They have denied God and said, 'It is not he.'"** Since, therefore, after the return from the Babylonian captivity, the Jews never denied the Lord God in word or deed through the practice of idolatry, it necessarily follows that they denied Him at that time by saying "He is not God" when they rejected the Lord Jesus Christ—the true God and Son of God—and declared that He was not the Messiah. Instead, they appointed for themselves two false Messiahs, one after the other. Therefore, in the same chapter of that prophecy, it says:

> A lion from the forest has struck them, a wolf of the deserts shall spoil them, a leopard watches over their cities; everyone going out from there shall be torn in pieces. <note>original Hebrew: הכם אריה מיער זאב ערבות ישדדם נמר שקד על עריהם כל היוצא מהנה יטרף</note>

This is: **"A lion from the forest has struck them, a wolf of the desert (or of the evening) shall devastate them, a leopard is watchful over their cities. Everyone departing from them shall be made a prey."** The gloss of Rabbi Solomon <note>Rabbi Solomon ben Isaac, known as Rashi (1040–1105), a preeminent medieval Jewish scholar.</note> explains this as follows: **"A lion from the forest struck them,"** meaning the Kingdom of Babylon. **"A wolf of the desert (or of the evening) shall devastate them"** through the Kingdom of the Medes. **"A leopard watchful over their cities"** through the Kingdom of the Greeks. **"Everyone departing from them shall be preyed upon"** by Edom, that is, through the Kingdom of the Romans. 

This is according to Rabbi Solomon. By this exposition, it clearly appears that from the point where Jeremiah says, **"Everyone departing from them shall be preyed upon"** by Edom (the Romans), everything that follows must be understood as the destruction of the Jews carried out by the Romans. For elsewhere these words are found: **"Take away the branches, for they are not the Lord's. For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me,"** says God. **"They have denied God and said, 'It is not He.'"** But the vine from which these branches or shoots were to be taken away because they were not God's was the entire house of Israel itself, according to what was said in Hosea 10: 

> Israel is a luxuriant vine. <note>original Hebrew: גפן בוקק ישראל (Gephen boqeq Yisrael)</note>

From all these points, it is manifest that the reason the Jews were to be destroyed by the Romans was that they would betray and deny God. Although there was also another cause for their ruin and eternal damnation: namely, that they were unwilling to receive the law of the Messiah.

## ## That the Jews were to be destroyed and condemned for eternity because they would not receive the law of the Messiah. Chapter IX.

### ### CAPNIO, <note>Capnio is the Greek-derived pseudonym of Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous Christian Hebraist and one of the speakers in this dialogue.</note>

<margin>GALATINUS <note>Petrus Galatinus, the author of the work and a speaker in the dialogue.</note></margin>
**I** beg you, reveal this cause as well through their own scriptures. For certainly the Jews were to be destroyed and eternally damned because they refused to receive the law of the Messiah, and utterly failed to listen to the Messiah himself. This is most clear from what is contained in the book <term>Midrash Tehillim</term> <note>original: "Midras tehilim"; a Jewish homiletic commentary on the Book of Psalms.</note> regarding that verse of Psalm 10: **Why, O Lord, do you stand far off? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?** <note>original Hebrew: למה יהוה תעמוד ברחוק תעלים לעתות בצרה</note> For it is read there as follows:

<margin>It is said:</margin>
> Rabbi Yohanan <note>A prominent 3rd-century sage in the Land of Israel.</note> said: For three years and a half the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence of God; the text uses "diuinitas" (divinity).</note> stood upon the Mount of Olives and cried out, saying: "Seek the Lord while he may be found." <note>Isaiah 55:6</note> But they took no notice. As it is said in the 65th chapter of Isaiah: <note>The text incorrectly cites chapter 66.</note> "I let myself be sought by those who did not ask; I was found by those who did not seek me." This is like a company of travelers who were walking along a road. As evening approached, a host <note>original: "hospes"; likely an innkeeper or watchman.</note> came to them, saying: "Take yourselves into the inn because of wild beasts and thieves." But they said to him: "It is not our custom to stay in an inn at night." After they had departed, the dead of night and darkness fell upon them. Returning, they asked the host to open the inn for them. But he said to them: "It is not the host’s custom to open the inn at night, for he does not admit anyone during the nighttime. At the time when I sought to receive you into the inn, you were unwilling; but now that you desire it, I do not wish to admit you." Thus said the Holy One, blessed be He: "Seek the Lord while he may be found. Return, you backsliding children." But there was no one who sought or returned. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: "I will go and return to my first place." <note>Hosea 5:15</note> But after they were handed over to the Kingdoms—which are compared to wild animals—they began crying out: "Why, O Lord, do you stand far off?" The Holy One, blessed be He, said: "I was sought, and you did not seek. Now you seek me, and I do not hear you. Measure for measure." As it is said: "And it came to pass that just as he called and they did not hear, so they shall call and I will not hear." <note>Zechariah 7:13</note>

That is to say, Rabbi Yohanan said: For three and a half years the divinity stood on the Mount of Olives, and cried out saying: "Seek God, while he may be found." And they did not care. Just as it was said in the 66th <note>Isaiah 65:1</note> chapter of Isaiah: "I have caused myself to be sought by those who did not ask, and I was found by those not seeking." This is similar to a company of travelers who were walking on a road. When evening drew near, a host came to them, saying: "Withdraw into the inn on account of wild beasts, and on account of robbers." But they said to him: "It is not our custom to stay in an inn at night." After they had left, the dead of night and darkness rushed upon them. And having returned, they asked for the inn to be opened for them by the host. He, however, said to them: "The host is not accustomed to open the inn at night, since he does not admit a man in the nighttime. At the time I sought to receive you in the inn, you were unwilling; but now you seek it, and I indeed do not wish to admit you." Thus spoke God, holy and blessed: "Seek God while he can be found. Return, you transgressing sons." And there was no one who would seek and return. God, holy and blessed, said to them: "I will go and return to my first place." But after they were handed over to the Kingdoms, which were compared to animals, they began to cry out: "Why, O God, do you stand far off?"

# BOOK NINE

...reach the number **Berith** <gloss>Covenant</gloss>, that is, of the pact or treaty. And then you will understand the secret of that text written in the 31st chapter of *Deuteronomy*:

> Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers, and this people will rise up and go whoring after the foreign gods of the land where they are going to be among them; they will forsake me and break my covenant which I made with them. <note>original Hebrew: "הנך שכב עם אבתיך וקם העם הזה וזנה אחרי אלהי נכר הארץ אשר הוא בא שמה בקרבו ועזבני והפר את בריתי אשר כרתי אתו."</note>

This means: *Behold, you will sleep with your ancestors, and this people will rise up, and will play the harlot after the strange Gods of the land, into which they enter to dwell in it. And they will forsake me, and make void my covenant, which I have made with them.* These are the words of Rabbi Nehumias <note>Nehunia ben HaKanah, a 1st-century sage to whom many early Kabbalistic works were attributed by later Christian scholars.</note>, who preceded the coming of our Redeemer by nearly fifty years.

For the explanation of these words, it must be noted that this Hebrew word **Berith** <gloss>Covenant</gloss>, which signifies a pact or treaty, contains the number 612 according to <term>arithmetic calculation</term> <note>This refers to Gematria, a Jewish system of assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters to find hidden meanings.</note> among the Hebrews. For it is written with four letters, each of which carries a certain number for them. For **Beth** (ב) signifies 2, **Resh** (ר) 200, **Yod** (י) 10, and **Tau** (ת) 400. Therefore, **Berith** (ברית), which is composed of these, contains 612. The names of the mother of the Messiah and her son also contain this same number (as we have shown elsewhere). For the name of the mother of the Messiah (as shown in the preceding sections by the same *Rabbenu Haccados* <gloss>Our Holy Teacher</gloss>) ought to be **Miriam** (מרים), that is, *Mary*. And the name of the Messiah her son, by which he was to be called by the Gentiles who would receive his faith, ought to be **Yeshu** (ישו), that is, *Jesus*. As the same *Rabbenu Haccados* previously showed. Now these names (namely **Miriam** <gloss>Mary</gloss> and **Yeshu** <gloss>Jesus</gloss>) also contain 612 according to Hebrew arithmetic. For **Mem** (מ) designates 40, **Resh** (ר) 200, **Yod** (י) 10, **Mem** (מ) 40, **Vav** (ו) 6, **Yod** (י) 10, **Shin** (ש) 300, and **Vav** (ו) 6. <note>The calculation is for "Maria and Jesus" (Miriam ve-Yeshu). In Gematria: 40+200+10+40 (Miriam) + 6 (and) + 10+300+6 (Yeshu) = 612.</note> And thus the names of the mother of the Messiah and the son, which are *Mary and Jesus*, contain the same number that the word **Berith** <gloss>Covenant</gloss> contains (namely 612). This same number is also carried by the words in the aforementioned text of *Deuteronomy* introduced by Rabbi Nehumias himself: **Elohe nechar ha-aretz** (אלהי נכר הארץ), that is, *the foreign gods of the land.* For **Aleph** (א) signifies 1, **Lamed** (ל) 30, **He** (ה) 5, **Yod** (י) 10, **Nun** (נ) 50, **Kaph** (כ) 20, **Resh** (ר) 200, **He** (ה) 5, **Aleph** (א) 1, **Resh** (ר) 200, and **Tsadi** (צ) 90. All of these together make 612.

From these things, therefore, the previously mentioned words of Rabbi Nehumias are clear when he says: *When you know the name of this rock (that is, the mother of the Messiah, which is Mary) and the name of her son (that is, the Messiah himself, which is Jesus), and that by arithmetic calculation they rise to the number of **Berith** (that is, the Covenant), which number is 612; then you will understand the secret of that text: "Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers," and the rest.* That was therefore a great secret which the Lord then revealed to Moses in the 31st chapter of *Deuteronomy*, saying: *Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers, and the people rising up will play the harlot,* along with the other things that follow. The sense of these words is indeed this: After you have departed from life, this people of yours will rise up and play the harlot (that is, they will err). Moreover, their error will be because they will say that Jesus and Mary are "the foreign gods of the land," that is, idolatries. And in this they will err, and they will forsake me, and they will make void my **Berith** (Covenant)—that is, my Jesus and my Mary—blaspheming them...

## That the Gentiles Were Bound to Cling to the Messiah. Chapter 12.

### CAPNIO,

<margin>GALATINUS</margin>
**S**ince you have spoken so much until now regarding the rejection of the Jews who persist in their <term>unbelief</term> <note>The Latin "perfidia" was a standard polemical term for the Jewish rejection of Christ</note>, it is fitting that you also bring forward something from the Hebrew scriptures regarding the calling and election of the Gentiles. Therefore, show first that the Gentiles themselves were to cling to the Messiah. GALATINUS: This is most clear from the fact that Zechariah prophesied in the second chapter that it would be so, saying: <note>original Hebrew: "ונלוו גויים רבים אל יהוה ביום ההוא והיו לי לעם"</note> *And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and shall be my people.* Which <term>Rabbi Jonathan</term> <note>Jonathan ben Uzziel, the traditional author of the Aramaic Targum of the Prophets</note> explains in his <term>Chaldean</term> <note>Aramaic</note> version thus: <note>original Aramaic: "ויתוספון עממין סגיאין קדם עמא דייהוה בעידנא ההיא ויהון קדמי לעם"</note> *And many peoples shall add themselves to the people of the Lord in that time, and they shall be my people.*

<margin>Objection of the younger Jews.</margin>
CAPNIO: Jewish impiety says here that the nations are to be added to God in the days of the Messiah not so that they may be saved, but so that they may serve the Jewish people.

<margin>Refutation.</margin>
GALATINUS: This falsehood of theirs is easily refuted. For just as God said concerning them in Leviticus chapter 26: <note>original Hebrew: "והתהלכתי בתוככם והייתי לכם לאלהים ואתם תהיו לי לעם"</note> *And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you shall be my people.* So also he says here of the Gentiles: *Many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and shall be my people.* From which it is clearly evident both from the divine page and from the <term>Chaldean</term> <note>Aramaic</note> translation that they are speaking entirely falsely. This is also expressly clear from the sayings of their own ancient Teachers. For it is read in <term>Massekhet Bikkurim</term> <note>The Mishnah tractate "First Fruits," which deals with the laws of bringing offerings to the Temple</note>, that is, in the book of the First Fruits, in this manner:

<margin>Tradition of Rabbi Judah.</margin>
The Masters handed down in the name of Rabbi Judah: That a <term>Ger</term> <note>original Hebrew: "גר"; a resident alien or proselyte</note>, that is a stranger—meaning a convert who comes from Gentility to the faith—is himself one who brings the first fruits and says those words in Deuteronomy chapter 26: <note>original Hebrew: "הגדתי היום ליהוה אלהי כי באתי אל הארץ אשר נשבע יהוה לאבותינו לתת לנו"</note> *I profess this day to the Lord your God, that I am come into the land which the Lord swore to our fathers to give us.* What is the proof of this? That which is written in Genesis chapter 17: <note>original Hebrew: "ולא יקרא עוד את שמך אברם והיה שמך אברהם כי אב המון גויים נתתיך"</note> *Neither shall your name anymore be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for a father of many nations have I made you.* For in the beginning he was the father of Aram, and therefore was called Abram. But afterward, he was the father of the whole world, and for that reason his name was called Abraham.

->Thus far<-

# BOOK IV

<margin>Jerome on this place.</margin>
Thus far the tradition. Moreover, **Rabbi Rahmon** <note>Likely referring to a Rabbinic authority or Midrashic source cited by Galatinus, possibly a variant of 'Rabbi Tanhuma' or similar</note> said regarding that which is spoken in Jeremiah, chapter 31: <term>וזרעתי את בית ישראל ואת בית יהודה זרע אדם וזרע בהמה</term> <note>original Hebrew: "And I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and the seed of beast."</note> That is: *And I will sow the house of Israel, and the house of Judah, with the seed of man, and the seed of beast.* The **seed of man** refers to those who are of Israel. Just as it is said in Ezekiel 34: <term>ואתם צאני צאן מרעיתי אדם אתם</term> <note>original Hebrew: "And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men."</note> This is: *And you are my sheep, the sheep of my pasture; you are men.* And concerning them, the holy and blessed God says in Isaiah 65: <term>והוצאתי מיעקב זרע</term> <note>original Hebrew: "And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob."</note> That is: *And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob.* However, that which follows, the **seed of beast**, refers to the converts from the nations, of whom it is said in the last chapter of Joshua: *And many cattle* <note>The author links "beast/cattle" to the Gentiles; the citation "Joshua ult." likely refers to Jonah 4:11 or a similar context of mercy toward cattle/outsiders</note>. And in Job, chapter 18, **Bildad the Shuhite** said: *Wherefore are we counted as beasts?* And concerning them, He says in Zechariah 2: *Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion. For behold, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, says the Lord. And many nations shall be joined to the Lord, and shall be my people.* Also concerning Israel and the nations of the world, the scripture speaks in Zechariah, chapter 8, saying: <term>כי לפני הימים ההם שכר האדם לא נהיה ושכר הבהמה איננה וליוצא ולבא אין שלום מן הצר</term> <note>original Hebrew: "For before those days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction."</note> This is: *For before those days the hire of man did not exist, and the hire of beast did not exist. And for him who went out, and for him who came in, or arrived, there was no peace from tribulation, or from the thresher.* **Before those days**, he means to say before the days of the Messiah; for in the days of the Messiah, there shall be peace for the far and the near.

As it is said in the fifty-seventh chapter of Isaiah: <term>בורא ניב שפתים שלום שלום לרחוק ולקרוב אמר יהוה ורפאתיו</term> <note>original Hebrew: "I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him."</note> That is: *Creating the fruit of the lips, peace. Peace to the far and the near, says God, and I have healed him.* <margin>St. Ambrose in ... <unclear>illegible</unclear></margin> Concerning him also, the scripture says in Zechariah chapter 9: <term>ודבר שלום לגוים</term> <note>original Hebrew: "and he shall speak peace unto the heathen [nations]."</note> This is: *And he shall speak peace to the nations.* For in that hour, there shall be peace for the one departing from this world through the way of <term>repentance</term>, and for the one entering, or coming before the holy and blessed God with good works and <term>almsgiving</term> <note>Latin: "eleemosynis"</note>. As it is said in Proverbs 14: <term>צדקה תרומם גוי וחסד לאמים חטאת</term> <note>original Hebrew: "Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people."</note> That is: *Righteousness exalts a nation, and mercy shall be for the nations against sin.* Where the glosses of **Rabbi Solomon** <note>Rashi</note> and **Rabbi Abraham Aben Ezra** say: the **righteousness** which the nations shall perform, and the **piety** which they shall return—that is, almsgiving—shall be for them in the place of sacrifice, and an atonement for sins. This is the tradition.

From all these things, it is clear that the nations were not to be added to the Messiah so that they might serve the Jews—as the Jews themselves, babbling in their delusions, gossip—but rather so that they might be saved and made the people of God. <margin>St. Augustine, Book 18 of *City of God*, chapter 28.</margin> Just as God Himself had foretold in Hosea, chapter 2, saying: <term>וזרעתיה לי בארץ ורחמתי את לא רחמה ואמרתי ללא עמי עמי אתה והוא יאמר אלהי</term> <note>original Hebrew: "And I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God."</note> This is: *And I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have mercy on her on whom I had not had mercy, and I will say to "not my people": "You are my people." And he shall say to me: "My God."* Moreover, that the Gentiles were to be saved in the time of the Messiah—who, receiving the Messiah himself, ought to confess him in heart, mouth, and deed—has been proved extensively above in the sixth book.

-> the Gentiles themselves would cling <-

# NINTH [BOOK]

### *That the Gentiles who receive the Messiah were to be loved by God and ought to be the chosen people of God. Chapter 13.*

#### CAPNIO,

**T**o the greater confusion of the Jews, therefore—who have been so shamefully rejected by God and held in eternal hatred—it must also be proved through their own scriptures that the Gentiles, in the time of the Messiah, being converted to the worship of the one and true God, were meant to be loved by God, and made into and called His chosen and special people.

#### GALATINUS,

This is most evident from the fact that, as a figure for this matter, God Himself commanded that proselytes—that is, those coming from the Gentiles to the worship of the one God—be loved in the Old Testament. Therefore, it seems by no means to be overlooked what is read in the book <term>Mekhilta</term> <note>original: "Mochilta"; a halakhic midrash or legal commentary on the Book of Exodus</note>, which is a certain exposition on Exodus. On that saying in the 22nd chapter of the same book [Exodus 22:21]: <term>וגר לא תונה ולא תלחצנו</term> <note>original Hebrew: "And a stranger you shall not wrong, nor shall you oppress him."</note> This means: *You shall not rebuke a stranger, nor shall you insult him, nor shall you oppress him,* specifically in matters of money. You shall not say to him: "Yesterday you were a worshiper of Bel <note>A Babylonian deity often used in these texts as a generic name for a pagan god</note>, and you were adoring his hollow idol, and even now, look, the flesh of pigs remains between your teeth! And yet you stand and speak before me?" And from where is it held that if you reproach him, he also can reproach you? From there, where it is said in Exodus chapter 22: *A stranger* (that is, a convert) *you shall not rebuke*, along with the rest.

Hence Nathan <note>Rabbi Nathan, a prominent second-century scholar of the Mishnah</note> used to say: "The blemish that is in yourself, do not speak of to your neighbor." For converts are beloved; for in every place there is a warning on their behalf, such as that in Exodus 22: *And a <term>ger</term>* <note>The Hebrew word for "stranger" or "sojourner," which in Rabbinic tradition specifically refers to a convert to Judaism</note>, *that is a convert, you shall not oppress.* And a stranger, that is a convert from the Gentiles, you shall not rebuke.

Rabbi Eliezer said: "Since the turning away of a stranger—that is, his conversion—is most difficult <note>The Latin 'pessima' (worst/most difficult) here likely refers to the spiritual and social fragility of the convert’s transition</note>, therefore the warning is given for him in many places." But Rabbi Simeon said: "Behold, God Himself says in Judges chapter 5: *And you shall love him as the rising of the sun in its strength.* For which of the two is greater: he who loves the King, or he whom the King loves? Behold, without a doubt they say: he whom the King loves!" Concerning whom it is said in Deuteronomy 10: <term>האל הגדול הגבור והנורא אשר לא ישא פנים ולא יקח שחד : עשה משפט יתום ואלמנה ואהב גר לתת לו לחם ושמלה</term> <note>original Hebrew: "The great God, the mighty, and the terrible, who regards not persons, nor takes a bribe: He executes the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loves the stranger, in giving him food and clothing."</note>

That is: *The great, strong, and terrible God, who does not accept faces* (that is, persons), *nor receives a gift; He performs justice for the orphan and the widow, and loves the <term>ger</term>*, that is, the convert from the Gentiles, *to give him food and clothing.*

Converts are also beloved. For in all things the <term>ger</term>, that is the convert, is named or described just as Israel is. For Israel indeed are called the "servants of God." The <term>hagherim</term> <note>The plural form of "ger," referring to converts</note>, that is the converts, are also called "servants of God." Just as it is said in Isaiah 56: *To love the name of God, that they may be His servants.* Israel was also called "ministers of God," as is said in Isaiah chapter 61: *You shall be called the ministers of our God.* And strangers also—that is, converts—are called "ministers of God," as is said in Isaiah 56: *And the sons of the foreigners joined to the Lord, to minister to Him.* Israel was also called "beloved," as...

<summary>Galatinus argues that Gentile converts (proselytes) were always intended to be part of God's chosen people, citing Rabbinic interpretations of Exodus and Deuteronomy. He emphasizes that God commands love for the convert and gives them the same titles—servant and minister—as the people of Israel.</summary>

# BOOK [IX]

...it was said in the first chapter of Malachi: *I have loved you, says the Lord.* They are also called 
<margin>strangers/converts</margin> 
<term>gherim</term> <note>original: "gherim"; Hebrew for strangers, often used specifically for converts to Judaism</note>, that is, beloved converts, according to what was said in the 10th chapter of Deuteronomy: *And he loves the stranger* <note>original: "gher"</note>, *giving him food and clothing.* Furthermore, the word <term>berith</term> <note>original: "berith"; Hebrew for covenant or treaty</note>, that is, a pact or league, was spoken of in relation to Israel, according to the verse: *And I will place my covenant in your flesh.* But this same word, *pact*, was also used regarding the <term>converts</term>, in the 56th chapter of Isaiah: *And the sons of the foreigners who join themselves to the Lord to be his servants, everyone who keeps the Sabbath so as not to profane it, and those who hold fast to my covenant, I will bring them into my holy mountain.* 

Moreover, it was said of Israel <term>raczon</term> <note>original: "raczon"; Hebrew for favor, goodwill, or acceptance</note>, which means "well-pleasing" or "complacency," as in the verse: *For their acceptance before the Lord.* This same term, *favor* or *complacency*, was also used for the converts in Isaiah 56: *Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be for* <term>favor</term> <note>original: "leraczon"</note>, *that is, for acceptance.* 

Furthermore, "guardianship" was spoken of regarding Israel, as in the 120th Psalm: *Behold, he who guards Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.* And guardianship was likewise spoken of regarding the <term>converts</term>, as in the 146th Psalm: *The Lord guards the strangers.* 

What more? Abraham called himself a <term>stranger</term> <note>original: "gher"</note>. As it is said in the 23rd chapter of Genesis, where he spoke to the sons of Heth, saying: *I am a stranger and a dweller among you.* David similarly called himself a stranger in the 39th Psalm, saying: *For I am a stranger with you.* 

This was done so that what was said in Isaiah 52 might be fulfilled: *The Lord willed, for the sake of his justice, to magnify the law and to extol it.* But he himself was entreated and plundered. And thus, in the 44th chapter of Isaiah, four types of <term>converts</term> are found responding and speaking before Him who spoke and the world was made—that is, Him who made the world by His word. For it is said: 

->This one shall say, "I am the Lord’s." This one shall call on the name of Jacob. This one shall write with his hand to the Lord, and shall be surnamed by the name of Israel.<- 
<note>original Hebrew: "זה יאמר ליהוה אני וזה יקרא בשם יעקב וזה יכתוב ידו ליהוה ובשם ישראל יכנה"</note>

This means: "This one shall say, 'I am the Lord’s,'" because he shall belong entirely to the Lord. "This one shall call on the name of Jacob"—these shall be the foreigners and those converted to justice, that is, to the Messiah. "And this one shall write with his hand to the Lord"—these shall be the men of repentance. "And he shall be surnamed by the name of Israel"—these shall be those who fear heaven, that is, those who fear God. 

Thus far the tradition. In this teaching, three reasons are assigned as to why those converted from the Gentiles to the worship of the one true God were to be loved. The first is because they are loved by God. The second is because in Holy Scripture they are named and treated by God in all things just as Israel is. The third is because the holy fathers and prophets, such as Abraham and David, called themselves strangers (that is, converts). 

Furthermore, the <gloss>commentary</gloss> of <term>Rabbi Solomon</term> <note>Rabbi Shlomo Yitzhaki, known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud</note> explains those same words of Isaiah cited at the end of this tradition as follows: *This one shall say, "I am the Lord’s"*—these shall be the perfectly righteous. *This one shall call on the name of Jacob*—these shall be the small children of the wicked. *And he shall write with his hand to the Lord*—these shall be the repentant men. *And he shall be surnamed by the name of Israel*—these shall be the <term>converts</term> <note>original: "hagherim"</note> from the Gentiles. For these things were explained in this way in the book <term>Avot</term> <note>original: "Auoth"; specifically referring to the "Ethics of the Fathers" or the related "Avot of Rabbi Natan"</note> by Rabbi Nathan. Thus says Rabbi Solomon. These preceding things are also most fitting...

# BOOK NINE

...is most fittingly connected to what is written in <term>Vaelle shemoth rabba</term> <note>original: "ואלה שמות רבה"; This is "Exodus Rabbah," a midrashic or interpretive commentary on the Book of Exodus</note>, that is, in the exposition of the Book of Exodus. Regarding that statement in chapter 12 of the same book: <term>This is the law of the Passover</term> <note>original: "זאת חקת הפסח"; Zot chukat hapessach</note>. For it is said there: This is what is written in the 56th chapter of Isaiah: <term>And let not the son of the foreigner, who has joined himself to the Lord, speak, saying: "The Lord will surely separate me."</term> <note>original: "ואאל יאמר בן הנכר הנלוה אל יהוה לאמר הברל יברילני יהוה"</note> For Job said in chapter 31: <term>The stranger shall not lodge outside</term> <note>original: "בחוץ לא ילין גר"; Bachutz lo yalin gher</note>, meaning the <term>convert</term> <note>original: "gher," which the author translates as "conversus"</note> shall not be kept out by the Holy and Blessed God. For what reason? Because the Holy and Blessed God does not exclude any creature, but receives everyone. For His gates are open at every hour, and whoever wishes to enter and be gathered, enters and is gathered. Because of this, it was said by Job: *The convert shall not lodge outside.* And again, it is said in the person of God, who is patient toward His creatures: <term>I will open my door to the traveler</term> <note>original: "דלתי לארח אפתח"; Dalti la'oreach eftach</note>.

Rabbi Berachias said: On behalf of whose person did Job say, "The convert shall not lodge outside"? Without a doubt, he said this because in the future, the <term>converts</term> <note>original: "גרים"; gherim</note> from among the Gentiles will be <term>priests</term> <note>original: "כהנים"; cohanim</note> ministering to the Holy and Blessed God. Just as it was said in Isaiah 14: <term>And the convert shall be joined with them, and they shall be gathered unto the house of Jacob</term> <note>original: "ונלוה הגר עליהם ונספחו על בית יעקב"; Venilvah hagher aleichem venispachu al beit Yaakov</note>. Moreover, "to be gathered" <note>original: "aggregari"</note> refers only to the status of priests. As it was said in the 2nd chapter of 1 Kings <note>modern 1 Samuel 2:36</note>: <term>Gather me to one of the priestly offices</term> <note>original: "ספחני אל אחת הכהנות"; Saphcheni el achat haccohanot</note>. For it shall come to pass that the <term>converts</term> from among the Gentiles shall eat of the <term>Bread of the Presence</term> <note>original: "הפנים"; happanim; literally "of the faces," referring to the Showbread in the Temple</note>, that is, the bread of proposition.

And thus he questioned the Masters, saying: What is it that was said in the 10th chapter of Deuteronomy: *And God loves the convert, giving him food and clothing*? Behold, all the confidence or promise with which God makes the <term>convert</term> <note>original: "hagher"</note> trust is that he might be given food and clothing. They said to him: Jacob, whose name is Israel, petitioned God in this way in Genesis 28: *If He will give me bread to eat and clothing to put on.* And for you, who have come to join us, is it not enough that you should be like us? Let it be enough for you that you are like us. Let it be sufficient for you that you are as Jacob, the firstborn of God. Finally, however, do not let the thought enter your mind that Jacob only asked for bread and clothing, or merely food and raiment. Because he said in addition: God made me confident that He Himself will be with me, and will make my offspring endure through the ages.

It follows, and this is what is written in the 2nd chapter of Zechariah: *Sing,* or *praise, and rejoice, O daughter of Zion, for behold, I come, and I will dwell in your midst, says the Lord. And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and they shall be my people.* All this is according to tradition. From these things it is clear enough that the Gentiles converted to God at the time of the Messiah were to be loved by God Himself, and ought to be called the 
->chosen people of God.<-

## That all honors once granted to the Jews were to be taken away from them, to be granted to the Gentiles who would receive the Messiah, as if to the true and chosen people of God. Chapter XIV.

->CAPNIO<- <note>Capnio is the scholarly pseudonym of Johannes Reuchlin, one of the characters in this dialogue.</note>

I do not by any means consider that it should be passed over here that it is proven through the Jewish scriptures that all the <term>honors</term> <note>original: "dignitates"; referring to spiritual privileges or status</note> once granted to the Jews were to be taken from them, as if from unworthy possessors, and granted to the Gentiles who would receive the Messiah, as if to the true, special, and chosen people of God. 

GALATINUS: This is shown most clearly through what is read in the <term>Midrash Tehillim</term> <note>original: "Midras tehilim"; This is a rabbinic commentary on the Psalms, also known as Midrash Shocher Tov.</note>, that is, in the exposition of the Psalms, regarding that statement in Psalm 75: *And I will cut off all the horns of the wicked, and the horns of the righteous shall be exalted.* <note>original: "וכל קרני רשעים אגרע תרוממנה קרנות צדיק"; The term "horn" in Hebrew scripture often symbolizes power, dignity, or strength.</note> For it says there as follows:

> It does not say "horn" [singular], but "horns" [plural]. For there are ten <term>horns</term> <note>original: "cornua"</note> that the Holy and Blessed God gave to Israel. 
> 1. The horn of **Abraham**, of whom it is said in Isaiah 5: *My beloved had a vineyard on a horn of the son of oil.* <note>The phrase "horn of the son of oil" is a literal rendering of the Hebrew for a fertile hillside.</note> 
> 2. The horn of **Isaac**, of whom it is written in Genesis 22: *And behold, a ram was caught in the thicket by its horns.* 
> 3. The horn of **Joseph**, that is, the horn of the Kingdom, of which it is said in Deuteronomy 33: *And his horns are the horns of a wild ox.* <note>The source text cites Deuteronomy 24, which is likely a scribal error for chapter 33.</note> 
> 4. The horn of **Moses**, of whom it was said in Exodus 34: *That the skin of his face was horned.* <note>original: "cornuta"; This reflects the Vulgate translation of the Hebrew "karan," which means "radiated light" or "shone," but was historically translated as "having horns," leading to the famous depictions of Moses with horns in medieval art.</note> 
> 5. The horn of **prophecy**, of which it was said in 1 Samuel 1: *And Hannah prayed and said, "My heart exults in the Lord, and my horn is exalted."* 
> 6. The horn of the **Torah** [Law], of which it is said in Habakkuk 3: *And there were horns coming out of his hand.* 
> 7. The horn of the **priesthood**, of which we read in Psalm 112: *His horn shall be exalted in glory.* <note>The text cites Psalm 111, following the Vulgate numbering.</note> 
> 8. The horn of the **Levites**, of which it was said in 1 Chronicles 25: *All these were the sons of Heman, the King’s seer in the words of God, to exalt the horn.* 
> 9. The horn of **Jerusalem**, of which it was said in Psalm 22: *And you have heard me from the horns of the unicorns.* 
> 10. And the horn of the **King Messiah**, of which it is said in the second chapter of 1 Samuel: *And he shall give strength to his King, and shall exalt the horn of his Messiah.* And so it says in Psalm 132: *There I will make a horn to sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for my Messiah.* 
> However, when Israel sinned, these horns were taken away from them and given to the nations of the world, just as...

<note>original: "Sicut"; catchword for the next page.</note>

<meta>This page continues the discussion from the previous page regarding the ten "horns" or symbols of power and dignity granted to Israel, and how they were allegedly transferred to the nations (Gentiles) following the rejection of the Messiah. It focuses on the interpretation of Daniel's vision of the fourth beast and the Midrashic commentary on Lamentations.</meta>
